occurrences.label: Blood Spiders are the true "glass cannons" of Kenshi. They are individually quite fragile, but they attack in groups, hit like a truck, and can walk along the bottom of bodies of water. Particularly in [The Swamp](/the-swamp), this means that being caught between Blood Spiders and a large lake can be a death sentence, as the spiders will simply follow a swimmer into the water and continue attacking them, unlike most pursuers. If faced on open terrain, however, it is relatively easy to outrun a pack. They are also quite weak to bleeding damage but can recover lost blood quickly. If you manage to down one, quickly looting its teeth to kill it is a good idea.

occurrences.label: They are large tan insectoid or arachnoid creatures with long, multi-jointed legs and a tiny, creepy head. They hunt anything nearby with high cutting damage attacks from their pointy legs, and they share their [smaller cousins'](/blood-spider) ability to "eat" their prey alive by draining its hunger bar.

occurrences.label: Although larger and tougher than Blood Spiders, Skin Spiders are generally less dangerous because they favor open terrain where they are easier to see coming and can fairly easily be outpaced. Like their cousins, they have high bleeding resistance and will wake up quickly should they be knocked out, so it is wise to loot their claws to kill them once downed.

occurrences.label: Standard Blood Spider swarms spawn in [The Swamp](/the-swamp), the [South Wetlands](/south-wetlands), and the [Burning Forest](/burning-forest). In The Swamp, there is a 20/75 chance of spawning a swarm of Blood Spiders, assuming that nothing has happened to nearby faction leaders. In the South Wetlands, there is a 1/9 chance of spawning a swarm of Blood Spiders, assuming that nothing has happened to the boss of the Red Sabres.

occurrences.label: When spawned at the [Southern Hive](/southern-hive-location), King will spawn with an age multiplier of 2.40x to 2.50x, bringing his effective skills well over 100. occurrences.label: Of note, the weapon selected randomizes every game load, using a seed generated from squad data. occurrences.label: **Crabs** are large, reddish, crustacean-like creatures that are usually hostile, perhaps because they are crabby. They are strong fighters but quite slow. They mostly roam coastal regions in the east/southeast parts of the continent, including the [Howler Maze](/howler-maze), [The Pits East](/the-pits-east), and [Greenbeach](/greenbeach). Their diet consists of fish, fungi, and algae.

occurrences.label: **Pack Beasts** are tamed [Garrus](/garru) used in Trade Caravans for [Nomads](/nomads), [Traders Guild](/traders-guild) and the [Western Hive](/western-hive) to haul supplies and materials in their [Garru Backpacks](/garru-backpack). They also make sturdy guards as they will happily participate in combat to protect their caravan. Despite their herbivorous nature in the wild, when tamed they are able to eat any kind of edible [food](/food), including [Foul Raw Meat](/foul-raw-meat). They also have a voracious appetite, eating enough for two humans. Pack Beasts can be purchased from [Nomad Animal Traders](/nomad-animal-trader).

They also make sturdy guards as they will happily participate in combat to protect their caravan. Despite their herbivorous nature in the wild, when tamed they are able to eat any kind of edible [food](/food), including [Foul Raw Meat](/foul-raw-meat). They also have a voracious appetite, eating enough for two humans. Pack Beasts can be purchased from [Nomad Animal Traders](/nomad-animal-trader).

occurrences.label: The Garru Backpack can carry goods in stacks of 6, which is one more than a Bull Backpack; they are otherwise identical in size, meaning an optimally-loaded Pack Beast can carry more stacked goods than its [Bull](/pack-bull) equivalent. However, the Garru Backpack has a built-in lantern that cannot be turned off except by removing the pack, so Pack Beasts make your party less sneaky at night. The light may potentially provide a boon to nocturnal crossbow users. Both Domesticated Bulls and Pack Beasts make sturdy combatants, though Garrus lack the powerful charge attack of the Bull. Overall, both species are great for hauling tons of materials even if they aren't the best fighters.

occurrences.label: If you have a Bonedog companion, keep in mind that units will not eat out of a bag until they reach 225 hunger. They will eat any food on the ground at 240 hunger as well as grab any [Severed Limbs](/severed-limbs) that are laying on the ground at 275 hunger to play with until they get bored shortly after and decide to eat it. The speed at which they get bored and decide to eat the limb is based off their age and hunger. If below 270 hunger and not currently fed (Hunger shown as <) it takes ~46 minutes of gametime for a player owned Bonedog to eat a limb if their age is under 0.9x. If the Bonedog is 0.9x or older it will not "play" with the limb, just keep it held in their mouth for a short period of time before eating it. If below 260 hunger the older Bonedogs will devour the limb instantly. All limbs provide 30 nutrients when eaten. Bonedogs can eat a limb before they reach 270 hunger (Common occurrence for an Elder Bonedog to grab a limb at ~275 hunger and then eat it a ~274) however as Hunger cannot exceed 300, the additional 4 nutrients will just slightly delay the time it takes to become hungry again. (As you do not lose hunger while "fed")

occurrences.label: Animal player characters cannot lose limbs. However, due to what is most likely an oversight, the limbs description will read that it is destroyed and useless like it would when a limb is lost for humanoids. In due time the limb will heal normally, despite the text. There aren't animal specific beds, however a humanoid player character can pick up an animal and place it in a bed manually. While animals are unconscious their heal speed is doubled. (Maybe due to a bug) If placed in a bed when unconscious an animal will only have their heal speed doubled until they regain consciousness. Many [Hostile Factions](/hostile-factions) (Bandit factions) will attempt to chop up your animals for food.

occurrences.label: All animals which can be purchased/controlled have something called "self healing". What this does is provided an animal is conscious their wounds will not degenerate, and they will automatically have bandaged health applied to them equal to 40% of the health they would normally heal.

occurrences.label: Although generally not aggressive, wild Garru can be skittish and may attack if the player or NPCs move around while very close to the herd. A party member with the Smart [personality](/personality) may comment, accurately, that standing still will prevent them from attacking. Simply keeping your distance is also effective. If a party member has the Maniacal or Dumb personality, they may taunt the Garru leading to a fight.

occurrences.label: -   [Garru](/garru) - Wild Garru may growl when the player moves nearby. If this happens and the player stops moving (disable jobs and press R) and remains still, the Garru will remain peaceful. However, if the player continues moving near them, the herd may attack. Depending on the personality of your character(s) they may insult the Garru provoking them to attack. The herd may also attack if another squad enters combat with the Garru. One of your characters will say something if the Garru might attack. letting you know to stop moving.

occurrences.label:
Note: Bandits May Butcher Animals
If players have animals in their squad and everyone gets KO'ed in battle, there's a high chance that bandits will butcher the animals for meat.

Animals can be made "unbutcherable" using an exploit: open the animal's inventory while they are unconscious, wait for them to regain consciousness and stand up (they must have a goal other than "getting up" and must not be unconscious or playing dead), and then remove the death items from their "unconscious" inventory. Prisoner cages can help restrain the animal during the process.

Prisoner cages can help restrain the animal during the process.

occurrences.label: When spawned at the [Southern Hive](/southern-hive-location), King will spawn with an age multiplier of 2.40x to 2.50x, bringing his effective skills well over 100. Important to note however that when hitting an animal, you gain XP through stronger opponent logic based off their stats when they are age 1.0 leading to very minimal XP. He is very tanky and is impossible to defeat solo without using Crossbows, microing or using [exploited recruited characters](/anti-slaver-jonin). However, when spawned as part of the raid that attempts to rescue the [Queen of the South](/queen-of-the-south), he will only spawn with a multiplier of 0.90x to 1.00x, making him pathetically easy.

occurrences.label: Being robotic, they are incapable of eating and will thus not eat your character upon KO. However, they usually don't leave the area as they typically spawn in fairly small, enclosed spaces, so be careful about getting back up if you regain consciousness. On top of all of this, they tend to spawn in groups, so fighting in a group against these can be a valuable strategy, if only to distract the spiders so they don't all prioritize one person. Be sure to spread out your characters as they can hit up to 2 units with each attack if they are close enough.

occurrences.label: -   Swamp Turtles also have an incorrect attack animation assigned to them. This means that, when players do take damage from them, they do not actually see the attack animation play. The attack animation also somewhat determines what type of attack the Swamp Turtles have, which in this case is supposed to be a stomp AoE attack. The mod, [Swamp Turtle FIX](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2237731365), resolves this issue by changing the attack animation to the correct one. Please note that by using the mod Swamp Turtles will be MUCH more dangerous.

occurrences.label: Aside from damaging the character inside of it, the Peeler Machine functions exactly like a [Prisoner Cage](/prisoner-cage). This means that placing any characters into them will count as imprisoning them, and any effects for imprisoning a character in a [Prisoner Cage](/prisoner-cage) (such as faction relationship changes) will also occur. However, if a character of any [faction](/factions) dies in a peeler machine, faction relations will not be affected any further. The Peeler Machine also produces [Animal Skins](/animal-skin) (somehow even from skeletons).
occurrences.literal: Aside from damaging the character inside of it, the Peeler Machine functions exactly like a [Prisoner Cage](/prisoner-cage). This means that placing any characters into them will count as imprisoning them, and any effects for imprisoning a character in a [Prisoner Cage](/prisoner-cage) (such as faction relationship changes) will also occur. However, if a character of any [faction](/factions) dies in a peeler machine, faction relations will not be affected any further. The Peeler Machine also produces [Animal Skins](/animal-skin) (somehow even from skeletons).

occurrences.label: The Peeler Machine works through 3 stages of its victim before it becomes inactive, if there is any clothing worn on the character, they will be destroyed by the peeler over time, after which the peeler will begin to deal cut damage to the victim's limbs. Once all limbs have fallen below 0 health it begins to deal damage to the characters vitals. It does not require the victim to be alive for this machine to work. Occasionally a peeler machine may bug and not damage a character's vitals even with all limbs below 0 health, and will stop damaging the vitals of a character if they are low enough.

occurrences.label: A selected player character can enter a prisoner cage by selecting the 'get in' option in the right-click-hold menu.
occurrences.literal: A selected player character can enter a prisoner cage by selecting the 'get in' option in the right-click-hold menu.

occurrences.label: To imprison a character which is not the selected player character, first pick up the target by opening the right-click-hold menu for the target and selecting 'pick up'. Carry the target to the cage and either place them inside it through right clicking the cage or use the right-click-hold menu for the cage and select 'put in'. The person will be dropped in the cage remain there until the cage is unlocked. Upon talking to the imprisoned character your relationship with his or her faction will drop by one.
occurrences.literal: To imprison a character which is not the selected player character, first pick up the target by opening the right-click-hold menu for the target and selecting 'pick up'. Carry the target to the cage and either place them inside it through right clicking the cage or use the right-click-hold menu for the cage and select 'put in'. The person will be dropped in the cage remain there until the cage is unlocked. Upon talking to the imprisoned character your relationship with his or her faction will drop by one.

occurrences.label: The fastest way for an imprisoned player character to exit a prisoner cage is through selecting 'escape' in the character's right-click-hold menu. This will initiate [lockpicking](/lockpicking) and the character will exit the cage as soon as they are able.

occurrences.label: Prisoner Poles are capturing devices used by [Cannibals](/cannibals), [Fogmen](/fogmen) and [Gurglers](/fishmen). [The Holy Nation](/the-holy-nation) also utilizes them in [Rebirth](/rebirth). When a recruit/NPC is captured nearby a prisoner pole they are locked in and eaten alive by the nearest enemies. This process can take anywhere from a few seconds to minutes, allowing for escape. They work a lot like [Prisoner Cages](/prisoner-cage) but with separate animations. They are also used by the [Southern Hive](/southern-hive). When tied up on a pole a character can medic themselves (Provided the job is set) once their legs reach a certain threshold. When eaten alive in Kenshi, cut damage as well as negative bandaged health is applied. You'll need to patch up that damage or your character will be crippled even with a full health robotic limb.

[The Holy Nation](/the-holy-nation) also utilizes them in [Rebirth](/rebirth). When a recruit/NPC is captured nearby a prisoner pole they are locked in and eaten alive by the nearest enemies. This process can take anywhere from a few seconds to minutes, allowing for escape. They work a lot like [Prisoner Cages](/prisoner-cage) but with separate animations. They are also used by the [Southern Hive](/southern-hive). When tied up on a pole a character can medic themselves (Provided the job is set) once their legs reach a certain threshold. When eaten alive in Kenshi, cut damage as well as negative bandaged health is applied. You'll need to patch up that damage or your character will be crippled even with a full health robotic limb.

occurrences.label: Compared to normal wheat farms, output seems low at first glance. However, as each plant produces 2 crops on harvesting, potential output is doubled. Maturation time is less than in a normal farm, so output per in game time gets to roughly half of an XL farm. More important, harvesting is much quicker for the Hydroponic, combined with less plants/more yield per plant, this results in a highly more efficient labour/output relationship, so are definitely recommendable for mid/endgame, if power is not a significant bottleneck. If Generators/Biofuel has to be used to power them, efficiency might be inferior, but no testing is done for this so far.
occurrences.literal: Compared to normal wheat farms, output seems low at first glance. However, as each plant produces 2 crops on harvesting, potential output is doubled. Maturation time is less than in a normal farm, so output per in game time gets to roughly half of an XL farm. More important, harvesting is much quicker for the Hydroponic, combined with less plants/more yield per plant, this results in a highly more efficient labour/output relationship, so are definitely recommendable for mid/endgame, if power is not a significant bottleneck. If Generators/Biofuel has to be used to power them, efficiency might be inferior, but no testing is done for this so far.

occurrences.label: A **Small Wind Generator** is a [building](/buildings-list) which produces [power](/power) via wind. After the initial cost of construction, Small Wind Generators generate power without any additional resource cost.
occurrences.literal: A **Small Wind Generator** is a [building](/buildings-list) which produces [power](/power) via wind. After the initial cost of construction, Small Wind Generators generate power without any additional resource cost.

occurrences.label: Small Wind Generators currently produce +0.25 power for every 1% of wind in the area, meaning a Small Wind Generator can generate up to a maximum of 25 power generated.
occurrences.literal: Small Wind Generators currently produce +0.25 power for every 1% of wind in the area, meaning a Small Wind Generator can generate up to a maximum of 25 power generated.

occurrences.label: Unlike the [Wind Generator](/wind-generator), the Small Wind Generator has an arbitrary number as a minimum amount of a wind required (1.12 mph) and is able to produce power nearly 100% of the time. The drawback to its reliability is that it has half the potential power output of the Wind Generator and a mere quarter of the upgraded Wind Generator II. Also unlike the [Wind Generator](/wind-generator), the Small Wind Generator may be built on the roof of [Player-Owned Buildings in Town](/player-owned-buildings-in-town), which might help if a town has a weak power grid, or the if player is planning to use a lot of power.

It can be used to automate the [Hunger](/guide-to-health#hunger) management of the units inside a [player-owned outpost](/guide-to-building-an-outpost) or [building in town](/player-owned-buildings-in-town).

occurrences.label: Comparably, wind farms will eventually require gargantuan amounts of space to power well-developed mid/late game bases and will need numerous [Battery Banks](/battery-bank) to ensure reliability during drops in wind-speed. occurrences.label: Compared to normal wheat farms, output seems low at first glance. However, as each plant produces 2 crops on harvesting, potential output is doubled. Maturation time is less than in a normal farm, so output per in game time gets to roughly half of an XL farm. More important, harvesting is much quicker for the Hydroponic, combined with less plants/more yield per plant, this results in a highly more efficient labour/output relationship, so are definitely recommendable for mid/endgame, if power is not a significant bottleneck. If Generators/Biofuel has to be used to power them, efficiency might be inferior, but no testing is done for this so far.

Despite the red-hued rain of [Vain](/vain) being understandably dubious, it is harmless and can be collected whereas places like the [Deadlands](/deadlands) or [The Unwanted Zone](/the-unwanted-zone)'s Acid Rain is hazardous and uncollectable. The Litmus test should be "Is the colored/acid rain deadly to an unprotected Human?" If no, harvestable. If yes, uncollectable.

occurrences.label: Small Wind Generators currently produce +0.25 power for every 1% of wind in the area, meaning a Small Wind Generator can generate up to a maximum of 25 power generated.
occurrences.literal: Small Wind Generators currently produce +0.25 power for every 1% of wind in the area, meaning a Small Wind Generator can generate up to a maximum of 25 power generated.

occurrences.label: Unlike the [Wind Generator](/wind-generator), the Small Wind Generator has an arbitrary number as a minimum amount of a wind required (1.12 mph) and is able to produce power nearly 100% of the time. The drawback to its reliability is that it has half the potential power output of the Wind Generator and a mere quarter of the upgraded Wind Generator II. Also unlike the [Wind Generator](/wind-generator), the Small Wind Generator may be built on the roof of [Player-Owned Buildings in Town](/player-owned-buildings-in-town), which might help if a town has a weak power grid, or the if player is planning to use a lot of power.

occurrences.label: This storage container was introduced in version 0.59.1 of Kenshi. Prior to that update the only way to store steel bars was to place them in a Storage Chest. This made automation of crafting more difficult because the player would have had to micromanage the input of steel bars or rely on the slow production of a [Steel Refinery](/steel-refinery). Initially the description for Storage: Steel Bars was the same as for the [Storage: Ore](/storage-ore). Back in version 0.59.1 there was no maximum capacity of steel bars that could be stored, but it was introduced later.

occurrences.label: Compared to normal wheat farms, output seems low at first glance. However, as each plant produces 2 crops on harvesting, potential output is doubled. Maturation time is less than in a normal farm, so output per in game time gets to roughly half of an XL farm. More important, harvesting is much quicker for the Hydroponic, combined with less plants/more yield per plant, this results in a highly more efficient labour/output relationship, so are definitely recommendable for mid/endgame, if power is not a significant bottleneck. If Generators/Biofuel has to be used to power them, efficiency might be inferior, but no testing is done for this so far.

occurrences.label: Armour gives Raw Iron (As long as it is made of Chain or Armour Plating) based off the coverage of the item. The amount of Raw Iron given is equal to (Chest Coverage/62.5(2/3)) + (Remaining coverage/62.5)

occurrences.label: If we use Samurai Armour as an example which has 100% Chest coverage and 85% Left arm, 85% Right Arm and 85% Stomach coverage it would result in (100/62.5(2/3)) + (255/62.5) = 2.4 + 4.08 = 6.48 Raw Iron. occurrences.label: In the world of Kenshi, much like the real world, **lighting** plays more than an aesthetic role and is a small but important factor to take into account when doing anything from collecting resources to waging war. Characters suffer a penalty when performing jobs without sufficient lighting, this applies to working a mine, a craft bench, or fighting, among other activities. It may seem like a small consideration, but if you are trying to craft high quality equipment you may find your character struggles during the night or take a penalty to their stats once the light fades away.

occurrences.label: General use containers can be used to store all types of items. Specialised containers (such as the Animal Feeder or an Armour Storage) are limited to containing a certain type of item. Specialised containers are [programmed](/jobs) to be used by labourers as input or output containers for various manufacturing processes. For example, a farmer might use the Fabric chest to store the [Fabrics](/fabrics) produced as output from crafting and a smith may use the same Fabrics chest to take the Fabrics to be used in clothes or armour production. Note that the specialised containers also clear the "[Stolen](/thievery)" tag from items when such an item is stored in a player-owned container, no matter how briefly.

occurrences.label: Security of an outpost completely surrounded by walls should be tested as enemies could glitch through them. To test this, the player should close the gates and order their characters to move to an area outside the walls to visualize the pathways their characters could take. No movement should indicate the walls are complete. Though the player's outpost may pass this test, enemies could still penetrate inside of a walled area if the walls are connected to elements of the world such as big rocks or mountain ranges. This is because constructed walls might not be completely connected to them. There is no way to safeguard these pathways except by pressing Shift+F12 to activate the game editor menu and by then constructing walls **inside** those "natural obstacles".

occurrences.label: ### The Gender Debate
occurrences.literal: ### The Gender Debate

occurrences.label: Skeletons, as a race, do not have biological sex. The game does not establish whether Skeletons possess or identify with a gender, and it is therefore debated whether the concept of gender identity applies to them at all. The general public commonly refers to Skeletons as male, seemingly as a default. Technically, the most accurate classification would be "neuter."
occurrences.literal: Skeletons, as a race, do not have biological sex. The game does not establish whether Skeletons possess or identify with a gender, and it is therefore debated whether the concept of gender identity applies to them at all. The general public commonly refers to Skeletons as male, seemingly as a default. Technically, the most accurate classification would be "neuter."

occurrences.label: The debate surrounding Agnu's gender identity originates from a single random biome dialogue entry[1], in which [Beep](/beep) asks, "Who else is female?" and Agnu responds with one of a set of randomly selected screams. The same set of screams is used as a word substitution for Agnu's otherwise incomprehensible speech throughout the game, with the specific scream being selected randomly rather than according to the context of the dialogue. For example, when the player attempts to take Agnu into [Venge](/venge), the same pool of screams is used in dialogue indicating that Agnu will not enter the area[2]. The screams therefore cannot be assigned a fixed meaning based solely on the dialogue in which they occur.
occurrences.literal: The debate surrounding Agnu's gender identity originates from a single random biome dialogue entry[1], in which [Beep](/beep) asks, "Who else is female?" and Agnu responds with one of a set of randomly selected screams. The same set of screams is used as a word substitution for Agnu's otherwise incomprehensible speech throughout the game, with the specific scream being selected randomly rather than according to the context of the dialogue. For example, when the player attempts to take Agnu into [Venge](/venge), the same pool of screams is used in dialogue indicating that Agnu will not enter the area[2]. The screams therefore cannot be assigned a fixed meaning based solely on the dialogue in which they occur.

occurrences.label: It has also been speculated that the response is related to Agnu's damaged state. This raises the question of whether the same response would occur after Agnu is repaired. However, interpreting the dialogue in this way can introduce real-world concepts that were likely not intended by the developers. There is no indication that the dialogue was intended to represent gender dysphoria or imply that such an identity constitutes being "broken." It might be more likely that the exchange was intended as a joke. The humor may simply come from the absurdity of attributing gender identity to robots in the first place.
occurrences.literal: It has also been speculated that the response is related to Agnu's damaged state. This raises the question of whether the same response would occur after Agnu is repaired. However, interpreting the dialogue in this way can introduce real-world concepts that were likely not intended by the developers. There is no indication that the dialogue was intended to represent gender dysphoria or imply that such an identity constitutes being "broken." It might be more likely that the exchange was intended as a joke. The humor may simply come from the absurdity of attributing gender identity to robots in the first place.

occurrences.label: The way the game handles Agnu's identity also suggests that the dialogue was not intended to establish a formal change in gender. There is no game mechanic or variable that changes after the exchange that would cause player characters or NPCs to subsequently refer to Agnu as "she." Referring to Skeletons as "he" is the general norm, and Agnu's character data identifies Agnu as male. Had the developers intended to formally establish Agnu as female, this could have been implemented through a simple change to the character's data.

There is no game mechanic or variable that changes after the exchange that would cause player characters or NPCs to subsequently refer to Agnu as "she." Referring to Skeletons as "he" is the general norm, and Agnu's character data identifies Agnu as male. Had the developers intended to formally establish Agnu as female, this could have been implemented through a simple change to the character's data.

occurrences.label: Therefore, Agnu is officially classified as male in the game's data, although some players interpret Agnu as female based on the mentioned ambiguous dialogue.

occurrences.label: These recruits can join the player for free. They are either rare finds due to spawn rates or have a chance to join the player after being freed from imprisonment. Some of these recruits retain bandit AI behavior or target designations and may potentially antagonize neutral travelers on the road or get attacked by guards or major faction patrols until the game is saved and reloaded.
occurrences.literal: These recruits can join the player for free. They are either rare finds due to spawn rates or have a chance to join the player after being freed from imprisonment. Some of these recruits retain bandit AI behavior or target designations and may potentially antagonize neutral travelers on the road or get attacked by guards or major faction patrols until the game is saved and reloaded.

occurrences.label: Mostly in [United Cities](/united-cities) territory, the player is able to purchase slaves from the [slave store](/slave-traders). The purchase is done in a similar way as with [buying animals](/guide-to-animals). Slaves can either immediately join the player after being freed or hang around for a while as "allies" before deciding to do so. However, unlike with animals, there is a chance of the slave abandoning the player immediately after purchase, or after some time of traveling together. This chance is lower with "stock" slaves found at the beginning of the game. Anyone found to be enslaved as part of the "living world" has a lesser chance to join the player.
occurrences.literal: Mostly in [United Cities](/united-cities) territory, the player is able to purchase slaves from the [slave store](/slave-traders). The purchase is done in a similar way as with [buying animals](/guide-to-animals). Slaves can either immediately join the player after being freed or hang around for a while as "allies" before deciding to do so. However, unlike with animals, there is a chance of the slave abandoning the player immediately after purchase, or after some time of traveling together. This chance is lower with "stock" slaves found at the beginning of the game. Anyone found to be enslaved as part of the "living world" has a lesser chance to join the player.

occurrences.label: **Mighty Canhead** is a unique character and a 'Magi' of the [Cannibals](/cannibals) faction. He will head a [Raid Event](/mighty-canhead-event) with 60+ other [Cannibals](/cannibal) if the player has an [outpost](/guide-to-building-an-outpost) in or near Cannibal lands. Mighty Canhead can also attack if the player has been causing a lot of trouble in the Cannibal plains, such as attacking the [Grand Cannibal Wizard](/cannibal-grand-wizard). If Mighty Canhead loses the assault, he will try again within 4 days. If he succeeds, there is a 10% chance that he will not return.

findings.verification: pinned imported claim identified; gameplay and technical semantics unverified
findings.finding: The imported trivia incorrectly calls 0xFFFFFF the maximum unsigned 64-bit integer and calls hexadecimal binary notation.
findings.proposedResolution: Correct the mathematical statement in a separate editorial change: 0xFFFFFF = 2^24 - 1 = 16777215; the unsigned 64-bit maximum is 2^64 - 1. Keep fictional cause and developer-intent speculation separate.
findings.uncertainty: The arithmetic discrepancy is established; the lore explanation remains speculation.
findings.postCutover: Serve the registered article with the imported qualification; keep this investigation open. Conversion is not gameplay verification.

occurrences.label: -   It is also the maximum value of a 64-bit unsigned integer in binary notation. This might imply that the bots' odd behavior is the result of an integer overflow error possibly caused by remaining active for hundreds of years without resetting.
occurrences.literal: -   It is also the maximum value of a 64-bit unsigned integer in binary notation. This might imply that the bots' odd behavior is the result of an integer overflow error possibly caused by remaining active for hundreds of years without resetting.

occurrences.label: **Hamut** is a [unique recruit](/unique-recruits) whose wife was taken by slavers. He can rarely be found in a bar in [Clownsteady](/clownsteady), [Drifter's Last](/drifters-last), or more commonly in [Shark](/shark-swamp-town). He is a potential recruit, costing nothing provided the interacting character opposes slavery. He can also spawn in other [UC](/united-cities) bars.
occurrences.literal: **Hamut** is a [unique recruit](/unique-recruits) whose wife was taken by slavers. He can rarely be found in a bar in [Clownsteady](/clownsteady), [Drifter's Last](/drifters-last), or more commonly in [Shark](/shark-swamp-town). He is a potential recruit, costing nothing provided the interacting character opposes slavery. He can also spawn in other [UC](/united-cities) bars.

occurrences.label: Hamut's opposition to slavery stems from his wife being taken as a slave. He has apparently contacted the Anti-Slavery Guild named [Spring](/spring), who failed to save his wife, and refused to recruit Hamut. Depending on the conversation choices, Hamut can state that he knows his wife is dead or imply that he believes she can still be saved. It is unclear which statement is true. Hamut does not refer to the site of his wife's incarceration by name- only mentioning that it is a mine.

occurrences.label: **Beep** is a Hiveless [Western Worker Drone](/hive-worker-drone) who can be found in [Mongrel](/mongrel). occurrences.label: We know far more about Armour King's shop than we know about Armour King himself. According to Armour King, he started his shop in a thriving Second Empire town called Catch nine-hundred thirty seven years ago. This coincides very nearly with the [fall of the Second Empire](/history-of-kenshi), yet Catch (a Second Empire town) was still thriving, meaning that the fall of the Second Empire likely didn't occur at a set date; it probably occurred over a very long period of time, with select towns falling into rebellion or disrepair, until eventually all that was left of the Second Empire was [Cat-Lon's Exile](/cat-lons-exile). This is further supported by what Armour King says about the collapse of the Second Empire.

This is further supported by what Armour King says about the collapse of the Second Empire.

Whether he took already broken skeletons or did [something more sinister](/skeleton-no-head-mkii) is not elaborated on.

occurrences.label: After the Red Rebellion, a new leader was chosen: Emperor Tengu, a starkly more impulsive man with a lack of common sense in comparison to his [predecessor](/puppet). As is tradition, Tengu has an ‘Inner Circle’ of four equally cruel, powerful, high nobles handpicked by himself. The emperor and his nobles are massively feared, particularly by the lower working class, and there are a huge number of rumors that reinforce this image, in particular stories of Tengu’s mysterious ‘Vault’ where rebels and enemies are sent.

occurrences.label: Slaves may sometimes be found wandering the map with their masters. This is true with [Noble Hunters](/noble-hunter) and [Reaver](/reavers) bands, the latter owning a special type of slave known as a [Reaver Slave](/reaver-slave). Freeing these slaves can also lead to potential recruitment, however one will most likely need to fight both the squad and the slaves themselves first, as their handlers can and will order these slaves to attack the player. This is always true for [Reaver Slaves](/reaver-slave), as their masters must be defeated in order for them to be recruited.

occurrences.label: Consequently, the scream used in response to Beep's question cannot be reliably interpreted as an affirmative response or as meaning "yes." It is unclear whether the response is intended as a joke or as a serious statement, or whether the response is even directly related to Beep's question. Since Agnu's speech is incomprehensible, the exact meaning cannot be established. The response could be an affirmative or negative answer, an unrelated reaction, or have no discernible meaning at all.

occurrences.label: It has also been speculated that the response is related to Agnu's damaged state. This raises the question of whether the same response would occur after Agnu is repaired. However, interpreting the dialogue in this way can introduce real-world concepts that were likely not intended by the developers. There is no indication that the dialogue was intended to represent gender dysphoria or imply that such an identity constitutes being "broken." It might be more likely that the exchange was intended as a joke. The humor may simply come from the absurdity of attributing gender identity to robots in the first place.

occurrences.label: **Berserkers** are members of the [Berserkers](/berserkers) faction. They can be found in [Berserker Village](/berserker-village) and patrolling [Stenn Desert](/stenn-desert), [Spider Plains](/spider-plains), [Berserker Country](/berserker-country), and [Cannibal Plains](/cannibal-plains). Taking down [Seta](/high-inquisitor-seta) can make them travel up to even [Okran's Gulf](/okrans-gulf), assuming [Ghost](/ghost) is alive and free.

occurrences.label: She is also capable of asking a squad of Anti-Slavers you encounter to bodyguard your squad for three days. occurrences.label: A few speculations could be made.
occurrences.literal: A few speculations could be made.

occurrences.label: - If a Skeleton character interacts with Elder, the only response that the said Skeleton can state in response to Elder's dialogue is that Stobe being "exterminator of the human plague" is a lie and that Elder himself is also aware of it.[4] This is verifiable as true given the existence of Humans in Kenshi (the "human plague" here seems to be referring to "humans as _the_ plague" rather than "plague that kills humans"). However, it's unclear if Stobe had the intention of exterminating humans but failed, or did not have such intention to begin with.

occurrences.label: -   In the same branch of dialogue above, Elder also states that calling Stobe "exterminator of the human plague" is a "justice" that is "ironic". It is unclear or at least not explicitly stated in what exact sense it's ironical in, who the target of retribution is, and if Elder wants Stobe to have recognition out of veneration or vilification for/against him.

occurrences.label: Not too far from where Stobe lay dead, you can find what appears to be a rocket or missile partially buried in the sand. Unlike most random space junk in the world, this world item seems deliberately placed. Perhaps this was the Ancients' contingency plan to end life on Kenshi following their collapse or abandonment of the island/planet, which Stobe sacrificed himself to stop. This would make more sense than a showdown where Stobe was 'killed' by an army or another Behemoth, as whatever killed him would then go on to kill the other races he tried to preserve.

occurrences.label: Killing the leader of a larger faction will not necessarily lead to the crippling of that faction. Instead, the player will need to find the other faction leaders and deal with them. These larger factions, such as [The Holy Nation](/the-holy-nation) and the [United Cities](/united-cities), will likely send increasingly strong [Base Assaults](/base-assault) if the player chooses to kill a minor faction leader before killing the primary leader, up until the point of the largest assaults, which would usually persist indefinitely and be launched every few days or weeks.

occurrences.label: If a character tied with homeless spawns was kidnapped or imprisoned but was later released, the homeless spawns tied with said character will all come back to effect. This appears to be intended as it likely accounts for successful rescue operations intended to bring their leader back alive[14], [Town Overrides](/town-overrides) may also switch in certain cases[15], in some cases it is even _necessary_ for the person needed to be initially killed/imprisoned to achieve the override to be _later released_ for the override to persist[16].

occurrences.label: -   Once they are allied, the bots will allow themselves to be picked up by player characters after a short time. This will bring two advantages that makes these characters invaluable. First, they allow themselves to be placed in [Prisoner Cages](/prisoner-cage), creating a "jack-in-the-box" kind of reserve military force. Being caged also keeps them away from neutral characters that these bots could otherwise attack. Second, once picked up, the bots can be equipped with new armour, weapons, and repair kits significantly extending their survivability and usefulness.

occurrences.literal: -   It appears that robotic patrols instead of only increasing in number, scales up activity immediately after Cat-Lon is taken down with all patrols 'On the run', evidenced by the fact that all of them move faster and static patrols are removed.

occurrences.label: -   Rather than causing an invasion when the leader is taken down such as the cases of [Esata](/esata-the-stone-golem) (causes [SK](/shek-kingdom) to [invade](/kamikaze) [HN](/the-holy-nation)) and [Hive Queen](/hive-queen) ([Southern Hive](/southern-hive) invading a significant portion of the world) or a diaspora such as the cases of [Phoenix](/holy-lord-phoenix) ([Strayed Paladin](/strayed-paladin)), [Tengu](/emperor-tengu) ([Samurai Rogue](/samurai-rogue)) and [Hive Queen](/hive-queen) ([Lost Hiver](/lost-hiver)/[Hive Bandit](/hive-bandit)), they simply patrol the same area more fervently than ever. This could either indicate them going berserk or trying to hunt down the one who took down their leader. Either way, it's going to be much harder to get out of the area unnoticed than when you got in.

occurrences.label: Holy Chosen can be found patrolling in large numbers making up the bulk of the Holy Army Force alongside some more experienced [Holy Sentinels](/holy-sentinel) and [Paladins](/paladin).
occurrences.literal: Holy Chosen can be found patrolling in large numbers making up the bulk of the Holy Army Force alongside some more experienced [Holy Sentinels](/holy-sentinel) and [Paladins](/paladin).

occurrences.label: They guard the [Shek](/shek) capital [Admag](/admag) and the city [Squin](/squin), and are found as patrol leaders leading [Shek Warriors](/shek-warrior). The patrols they lead are consisted of 1 ~ 2 Hundred Guardians, and 4 ~ 8 Shek Warriors. They also serve as police inside Shek Kingdom towns.

occurrences.label: If the player is allied with [The Holy Nation](/the-holy-nation), their patrols will attack the player unprovoked (unless the player is allied with them too).
occurrences.literal: If the player is allied with [The Holy Nation](/the-holy-nation), their patrols will attack the player unprovoked (unless the player is allied with them too).

occurrences.label: Once allied with the Shek Kingdom, a player can talk to wandering patrols of **Hundred Guardians** to ask them to bodyguard the player or guard their outpost. They will then follow the player for 72 hours or guard their outpost for 48 hours.
occurrences.literal: Once allied with the Shek Kingdom, a player can talk to wandering patrols of **Hundred Guardians** to ask them to bodyguard the player or guard their outpost. They will then follow the player for 72 hours or guard their outpost for 48 hours.

occurrences.label: Note that the Hundred Guardians guarding towns can be talked to but will refuse to follow, redirecting the player to look for patrolling Hundred Guardians outside Shek cities.
occurrences.literal: Note that the Hundred Guardians guarding towns can be talked to but will refuse to follow, redirecting the player to look for patrolling Hundred Guardians outside Shek cities.

occurrences.label:
1. ↑ "They have same stats of a Hundred Guardian"
  2. ↑ One of the patrol spawns tied with Esata in Stenn Desert de-spawns when she is killed, suggesting that they went Kamikaze
  3. ↑ Admag's complete destruction and depopulation is tied directly with Esata
  4. ↑ High Inquisitor Valtena for one is hinted by Moll to have significant patrol presence in Okran's Pride, despite there being no homeless spawn patrols in that area tied to him when he is alive.
  5. ↑ Border Zone for example is hinted to have High Inquisitor Seta's forces blocking Shek Kingdom as his status is tied with the latter's patrol presence in the area, even when they are clearly launching assaults into Okran's Pride and Okran's Gulf when Seto is dead.
  6. ↑ High Inquisitor Seta and Holy Lord Phoenix's status prevents Kral's Chosen from spawning in Skinner's Roam despite not having any simulated patrol presence in the area (initially), suggesting they have some level of army force there that aren't simulated.
  7. ↑ Esata's status has zero effects on whether or not Holy Farms get destroyed. The farmers will even be reliefed if Esata is incapacitated. This suggests that the Sheks could easily be spreading themselves too thin to be effective if they launch full front assaults as Kamikaze.
  8. ↑ Holy Farmers would cease to complain about tribute extortions if Esata is killed/kidnapped, even if Seta, Phoenix and Valtena are all dead by this point, suggesting HN have mounted a successful defense against Kamikaze assaults that prevented further tribute raids.
  9. ↑ "Soon we'll purge the last of her beasts... Before the barbarians reach our gates for blood like the psychopaths they are." - Paladin
  10. ↑ "The horned devils plague the Holy Lands but they are small in number, they won't last with their wreckless suicide mission. Eventually their kind will be extinct and we'll finally see peace." - Holy Lord Phoenix
  11. ↑ "All you need to do is assassinate the Stone Golem, sir. Take her out of the picture and the Shek will surely fight themselves extinct"
  12. ↑ "The Shek devils are in turmoil. They still linger on, one cannot simply plug the dark abyss closed of it's inner evils, but their threat is considerably lessened..." - Holy Lord Phoenix

occurrences.label: They appear to be [Paladins](/paladin) who are separated from Holy Nation's military leadership and roam aimlessly in the wilds. They tend to equip a variety of makeshift rags and armor, somewhat similar to [Starving Bandits](/starving-bandits). Unlike [them](/hungry-bandit), however, they are _not_ malnourished and are still formidable in combat. They have the same stats as a [Paladin](/paladin), as well as a Smart [Personality](/personality).

occurrences.label: A [United Cities](/united-cities) citizen, Cat was dressed very nicely on his way to a date when he was mistaken for a rich person because of his nice clothes. He got caught by the [Dust Bandits](/dust-bandits). They wanted a ransom for him because they thought he was someone important, but no one showed up, so he was left in prison in the [Dust King Tower](/dust-king-tower). occurrences.label: **Unique Recruits** are unique [Playable Characters](/playable-characters) that can only ever appear once per game unless imported. They have dialogue unique to them and often have higher [stats](/statistics) than average [recruits](/generic-recruits), a few of them may even be tied to [World States](/world-states). While most unique recruits are just found in bars and often require a fee to hire, this is not necessarily true for all of them. Note that if a recruit has unique dialogue and joins the player's faction, the dialogue will remain even after the character's name or body shape has been changed via the [Plastic Surgeon](/plastic-surgeon).

occurrences.label: ## Buying Slaves
occurrences.literal: ## Buying Slaves

occurrences.label: Mostly in [United Cities](/united-cities) territory, the player is able to purchase slaves from the [slave store](/slave-traders). The purchase is done in a similar way as with [buying animals](/guide-to-animals). Slaves can either immediately join the player after being freed or hang around for a while as "allies" before deciding to do so. However, unlike with animals, there is a chance of the slave abandoning the player immediately after purchase, or after some time of traveling together. This chance is lower with "stock" slaves found at the beginning of the game. Anyone found to be enslaved as part of the "living world" has a lesser chance to join the player.
occurrences.literal: Mostly in [United Cities](/united-cities) territory, the player is able to purchase slaves from the [slave store](/slave-traders). The purchase is done in a similar way as with [buying animals](/guide-to-animals). Slaves can either immediately join the player after being freed or hang around for a while as "allies" before deciding to do so. However, unlike with animals, there is a chance of the slave abandoning the player immediately after purchase, or after some time of traveling together. This chance is lower with "stock" slaves found at the beginning of the game. Anyone found to be enslaved as part of the "living world" has a lesser chance to join the player.

occurrences.label: There's a way to recruit some of the non-recruitable characters by "buying their freedom" after they are enslaved. The irony of this method is in that it is **the player** that puts them into this terrible situation and then "rescues" them. Players should pick up **unconscious** characters, travel to the slavers, and then **drop them down in front of the slavers** so that they'd enslave them. After it is done, it is safe to "rescue" the new slaves by buying their freedom. Provided that the player characters are not seen by the new slaves prior to them suddenly appearing in a slave cage and with a headache, they will feel grateful towards the player. Upon being freed, some former slaves will join the player's party as a form of gratitude. This strategy has been tested on [Holy Nation Robots](/holy-nation-robot) for example.

occurrences.label: Slaves may sometimes be found wandering the map with their masters. This is true with [Noble Hunters](/noble-hunter) and [Reaver](/reavers) bands, the latter owning a special type of slave known as a [Reaver Slave](/reaver-slave). Freeing these slaves can also lead to potential recruitment, however one will most likely need to fight both the squad and the slaves themselves first, as their handlers can and will order these slaves to attack the player. This is always true for [Reaver Slaves](/reaver-slave), as their masters must be defeated in order for them to be recruited.

occurrences.literal: **Agnu** is a [Unique Recruit](/unique-recruits) who can be found imprisoned by the [Thrall Masters](/thrall-masters) in the top floor of the [Tower of Abuse](/tower-of-abuse). occurrences.label: -   You can rush to the Tower of Abuse on day one with a pair of tools/hacksaws (Or two if you care about your starting character) to free Agnu. If this fails to work, save and load your game to cause enemies to behave normally as recruiting a character can cause some weird AI behavior.)

occurrences.label: **Green Finger** is a [Unique Recruit](/unique-recruits) who can be found in [Fishing Village](/fishing-village-northern-coast). occurrences.label: **Griffin** is a [Unique Recruit](/unique-recruits) found in any [Holy Nation](/the-holy-nation) bar. He believes he had a vision from [Okran](/okran), who showed him that he would meet a wealthy wanderer, and that wanderer would lead him to the truth of the First Extinction. Whether or not you believe him, he believes this wanderer is you and asks for c.9,000 as proof of your wealth.

occurrences.label: He is a very good human recruit for melee combat, as he has a 20 for melee attack and defence, a 20 in all melee weapon stats except polearms, and a 20 in strength and dexterity. This makes him a reliable and very versatile recruit for combat purposes, as he can competently use almost any melee weapon without having to train his stats first, although keep in mind his non-combat stats are abysmal, so there will be a time investment required if you plan to use him for something like mining or farming in-between fighting. It's also worth noting that his athletics skill is also 20, which is plenty enough to outrun enemies like [Starving Bandits](/starving-bandits) and [Fogmen](/fogmen).

occurrences.label: **Hamut** is a [unique recruit](/unique-recruits) whose wife was taken by slavers. He can rarely be found in a bar in [Clownsteady](/clownsteady), [Drifter's Last](/drifters-last), or more commonly in [Shark](/shark-swamp-town). He is a potential recruit, costing nothing provided the interacting character opposes slavery. He can also spawn in other [UC](/united-cities) bars.

occurrences.label: Hamut's opposition to slavery stems from his wife being taken as a slave. He has apparently contacted the Anti-Slavery Guild named [Spring](/spring), who failed to save his wife, and refused to recruit Hamut. Depending on the conversation choices, Hamut can state that he knows his wife is dead or imply that he believes she can still be saved. It is unclear which statement is true. Hamut does not refer to the site of his wife's incarceration by name- only mentioning that it is a mine.

They have a unique recruitment dialogue that may become available when they see a player character and the following conditions are met:

occurrences.label: -   Their Strength, Dexterity, Melee Attack, Melee Defence, Martial Arts, and Dodge are all less than 25 or the cumulative total of these statistics is less than 75. (In FCS this condition is named DC\_IS\_RECRUITABLE).
occurrences.literal: -   Their Strength, Dexterity, Melee Attack, Melee Defence, Martial Arts, and Dodge are all less than 25 or the cumulative total of these statistics is less than 75. (In FCS this condition is named DC\_IS\_RECRUITABLE).

occurrences.label: This is a rare occurrence given their base statistics, which often causes them to exceed the recruitable threshold. If all the triggering conditions are met however and they see the player, they will say aloud "He/She saw me ..." followed by "... Do what you will, human ..." At that point, they can be clicked on to initiate further dialogue, just like when other NPCs make announcements. Offering to help them repair their damage in this dialogue (regardless of whether they actually have any injuries) and proclaiming defiance of the Holy Nation will result in recruitment. Stating that you just like helping people and have no hidden agenda though will result in the dialogue ending without recruitment.

occurrences.label: -   There is a 48 internal hour cooldown after the Holy nation robot dialogue is triggered. occurrences.label: **Ray** is a [Unique Recruit](/unique-recruits). He is a mute slave who can be bought for c.1,000 from [Bar fly](/bar-fly) at either [Eyesocket](/eyesocket) in the [Stormgap Coast](/stormgap-coast), or the [Slave Markets](/slave-markets) in the [South Wetlands](/south-wetlands). Until recruited he is a member of the [Outlaw](/outlaw) faction. If you kill Bar fly before buying Ray, you won't be able to recruit him.

occurrences.label: The player can also question if she is in the cult of Narko, where she will firstly laugh and insult HN's teachings and then give her own idea that HN is just one of many possibilities in a religion and say that they fight Holy army because of those labels. She will then go on a rant about religion if the player wants to hear about it, where the player could choose to stop her and move to other topics, allow her to go on the rant, or attempt an 'Okran's Crusade'. If the player allowed her to move on her rant, she will say that many of the ninjas that escaped HN still believe in Okran but an aspect without good and evil, but to her it's all nonsense. The player can then agree with her viewpoint which will give the player +3 relation points with FN, ignore her or attempt 'Okran's Crusade' (again).

occurrences.label: -   Due to their very high base stats and decent stat randomization certain races can spawn with stats past the max level achievable by leveling. Many of these skills can actually continue to level again due to how the experience curve works. This makes recruiting an Anti-Slaver extremely game breaking. The following races can spawn with "break" stats, and the max random stat they can spawn with. (Note not all stats over 100 can continue to level, all "combat" stats listed can but others will need more testing to verify. Not including Field Medic as it can go beyond 100 normally)

occurrences.label: She can be found lamenting their purchase of [Ray](/ray) and considering making goat-feed out of him due to his uselessness. Not only does the slave have no tongue and thus cannot speak, they are also stubborn, lazy and feisty. The player can offer c.1000 to take Ray out of Bar fly's hands and gain them as a [Unique Recruit](/unique-recruits). Two or more bar flies may spawn spontaneously in different locations, and the dialogue of selling Ray may still be available on the other bar flies even if you have already bought Ray, albeit there won't be another Ray for sale as Ray only spawn once in each playthrough.

occurrences.label: Her character is based upon a fanfiction written by a supporter of the game, you can find the [full original backstory here](https://steamcommunity.com/app/233860/discussions/4/611704531888528365/#c350532536102110190). In it, she was born into a wealthy family of [The Holy Nation](/the-holy-nation), her parents were killed by [Skeletons](/skeletons) during a night journey from [Stack](/stack) to [Blister Hill](/blister-hill). When she was found by a passing [Paladin](/paladin) patrol, she was promptly put to [slavery](/slavery) by an [Inquisitor](/inquisitor) for penance. She spent years plotting an escape, and her hatred of men intensified as more abuses and attention were given to her as she came of age.

occurrences.label: **Lower Servants** are [Slaves](/slaves) within [The Holy Nation](/the-holy-nation), usually working in one of the many [Holy Mine](/holy-mines) sites. They are likely criminals (like [Starving Bandits](/starving-bandits) and [Dust Bandits](/dust-bandits)) that are [enslaved](/slavery) for repentance and prison labor.

occurrences.label: Lower Servants may be recruited once freed; they will follow the player for some time, before engaging in dialogue. Given certain dialogue choices, the Player can either part with them or allow them to join their squad. Note that they will have the "Slave of" Holy Nation and "Looks Like Slave" percentage tied to their character for some time following their recruitment. Giving them proper armour and clothing will help protect them until the two tags eventually go away.

occurrences.label: Occasionally, if there are no witnesses, they will attempt to attack and capture freemen to pass them off as escaped slaves even if doing so is clearly a very bad idea. occurrences.label: **Slave Hunters** are members of the faction of [Slave Hunters](/slave-hunters). occurrences.label: **Fog Princes** are the leaders of the [Fogmen](/fogmen) faction. They each have a head which can be removed from their inventory and sold for a bounty of c.6,000. Fog Princes are never alone in the wild, often surrounded by [Fogmen](/fogman) and [Fog Heavies](/fog-heavy). Seeking the Princes out in the fog, even with several well-equipped combatants, can be very unforgiving.

occurrences.label: Like [Miu](/miu) who spots spiders, Pia is always on alert for Holy Paladins, acting as a useful radar for the group. She is the fastest paid recruit ([Bo](/bo) is faster but requires much more to recruit and is free) having a massive 50 Athletics along with a modest 20 Strength/Dexterity.

findings.finding: Slavery recruitment describes different purchase and liberation rules, while free recruits may retain hostile AI until reload.
findings.proposedResolution: Test purchase and liberation separately with exact dialogue packages, personalities and prior player hostility; preserve method distinctions.
findings.uncertainty: The buying-freedom workaround must not be generalized to liberation, and reload/import claims need version-specific tests.
findings.postCutover: Serve the registered article with the imported qualification; keep this investigation open. Conversion is not gameplay verification.

occurrences.label: There's a way to recruit some of the non-recruitable characters by "buying their freedom" after they are enslaved. The irony of this method is in that it is **the player** that puts them into this terrible situation and then "rescues" them. Players should pick up **unconscious** characters, travel to the slavers, and then **drop them down in front of the slavers** so that they'd enslave them. After it is done, it is safe to "rescue" the new slaves by buying their freedom. Provided that the player characters are not seen by the new slaves prior to them suddenly appearing in a slave cage and with a headache, they will feel grateful towards the player. Upon being freed, some former slaves will join the player's party as a form of gratitude. This strategy has been tested on [Holy Nation Robots](/holy-nation-robot) for example.

occurrences.label: Bar squads such as the recruits shown on this page will **not** respawn or change over time. If you have emptied a bar, or they got killed, do not expect it to refill at some point. An [import](/main-menu) must be performed for any of them to refill.

occurrences.label: These recruits can join the player for free. They are either rare finds due to spawn rates or have a chance to join the player after being freed from imprisonment. Some of these recruits retain bandit AI behavior or target designations and may potentially antagonize neutral travelers on the road or get attacked by guards or major faction patrols until the game is saved and reloaded.

occurrences.label: description: "The Armour King is a Skeleton merchant who sells Armour gear in Armour King's Shop. He is a masterful armoursmith who produces high-end armor to give travele…"
occurrences.literal: description: "The Armour King is a Skeleton merchant who sells Armour gear in Armour King's Shop. He is a masterful armoursmith who produces high-end armor to give travele…"

occurrences.label: The **Armour King** is a [Skeleton](/skeleton) merchant who sells [Armour](/armour) gear in [Armour King's Shop](/armour-kings-shop). He is a masterful armoursmith who produces high-end armor to give travelers superior protection.
occurrences.literal: The **Armour King** is a [Skeleton](/skeleton) merchant who sells [Armour](/armour) gear in [Armour King's Shop](/armour-kings-shop). He is a masterful armoursmith who produces high-end armor to give travelers superior protection.

occurrences.label: -   The Armour Kings shop is the only place to find Masterwork Hive Shirt Armour. In fact, it is the only shop to sell Masterwork Armour naturally. Other shops which sell Masterwork quality armour are just artifact spawns and will not spawn again once purchased.
occurrences.literal: -   The Armour Kings shop is the only place to find Masterwork Hive Shirt Armour. In fact, it is the only shop to sell Masterwork Armour naturally. Other shops which sell Masterwork quality armour are just artifact spawns and will not spawn again once purchased.

occurrences.label: -   Armour King's shop will spawn between 32 to 48 pieces of armour every time he restocks.
occurrences.literal: -   Armour King's shop will spawn between 32 to 48 pieces of armour every time he restocks.

occurrences.label: Mostly in [United Cities](/united-cities) territory, the player is able to purchase slaves from the [slave store](/slave-traders). The purchase is done in a similar way as with [buying animals](/guide-to-animals). Slaves can either immediately join the player after being freed or hang around for a while as "allies" before deciding to do so. However, unlike with animals, there is a chance of the slave abandoning the player immediately after purchase, or after some time of traveling together. This chance is lower with "stock" slaves found at the beginning of the game. Anyone found to be enslaved as part of the "living world" has a lesser chance to join the player.
occurrences.literal: Mostly in [United Cities](/united-cities) territory, the player is able to purchase slaves from the [slave store](/slave-traders). The purchase is done in a similar way as with [buying animals](/guide-to-animals). Slaves can either immediately join the player after being freed or hang around for a while as "allies" before deciding to do so. However, unlike with animals, there is a chance of the slave abandoning the player immediately after purchase, or after some time of traveling together. This chance is lower with "stock" slaves found at the beginning of the game. Anyone found to be enslaved as part of the "living world" has a lesser chance to join the player.

occurrences.label: **Unique Recruits** are unique [Playable Characters](/playable-characters) that can only ever appear once per game unless imported. They have dialogue unique to them and often have higher [stats](/statistics) than average [recruits](/generic-recruits), a few of them may even be tied to [World States](/world-states). While most unique recruits are just found in bars and often require a fee to hire, this is not necessarily true for all of them. Note that if a recruit has unique dialogue and joins the player's faction, the dialogue will remain even after the character's name or body shape has been changed via the [Plastic Surgeon](/plastic-surgeon).

occurrences.label: Hamut's opposition to slavery stems from his wife being taken as a slave. He has apparently contacted the Anti-Slavery Guild named [Spring](/spring), who failed to save his wife, and refused to recruit Hamut. Depending on the conversation choices, Hamut can state that he knows his wife is dead or imply that he believes she can still be saved. It is unclear which statement is true. Hamut does not refer to the site of his wife's incarceration by name- only mentioning that it is a mine.

occurrences.label:
WANTED: Giant King Gurgler
WANTED for crimes of kidnapping and cannibalism of Catun residents.

Neither man nor animal, the Giant King Gurgler is an enormous beast with more similarity to a hiveman-crossed-crab, ten-fold in size.

Wanted dead. Thought to be dwelling south of Catun's shore. Head required as proof.

UPDATE:The King Gurgler has been reported to be in possession of an ancient weapon of the fallen empire. Assassinate him and the weapon is yours to keep.
REWARD:c.60,000

  2. ↑ One of the patrol spawns tied with Esata in Stenn Desert de-spawns when she is killed, suggesting that they went Kamikaze
  3. ↑ Admag's complete destruction and depopulation is tied directly with Esata
  4. ↑ High Inquisitor Valtena for one is hinted by Moll to have significant patrol presence in Okran's Pride, despite there being no homeless spawn patrols in that area tied to him when he is alive.

occurrences.label: Not too far from where Stobe lay dead, you can find what appears to be a rocket or missile partially buried in the sand. Unlike most random space junk in the world, this world item seems deliberately placed. Perhaps this was the Ancients' contingency plan to end life on Kenshi following their collapse or abandonment of the island/planet, which Stobe sacrificed himself to stop. This would make more sense than a showdown where Stobe was 'killed' by an army or another Behemoth, as whatever killed him would then go on to kill the other races he tried to preserve.

occurrences.label: The players can influence the world of [Kenshi](/kenshi) in a number of ways. The most prominent (and straightforward) is the killing or kidnapping of the [important leader(s) of factions](/category/bosses). For a smaller faction (such as the [Skin Bandits](/skin-bandits)), killing their leader can lead to a vast reduction in the spawn rate for squads of that faction. The faction base is then destroyed or occupied by a different faction. Several of the factions may themselves also have questlines that may be part of one or many [Routes](/world-state-routes) which require certain achievements of World States.

The faction base is then destroyed or occupied by a different faction. Several of the factions may themselves also have questlines that may be part of one or many [Routes](/world-state-routes) which require certain achievements of World States.

occurrences.label: Generally speaking, it doesn't matter whether you Imprison or Kill a faction leader, the results will remain the same except in a few cases[1][2]. When certain condition states that it requires a person to be dead, imprisoning said character will also work. Conversely, if a condition states that it requires a person to be alive, it means that they should be alive AND free (not imprisoned). If (in [FCS](/forgotten-construction-set)) a condition checks whether or not a person is "Okay", it means whether or not they are both alive AND free.
occurrences.literal: Generally speaking, it doesn't matter whether you Imprison or Kill a faction leader, the results will remain the same except in a few cases[1][2]. When certain condition states that it requires a person to be dead, imprisoning said character will also work. Conversely, if a condition states that it requires a person to be alive, it means that they should be alive AND free (not imprisoned). If (in [FCS](/forgotten-construction-set)) a condition checks whether or not a person is "Okay", it means whether or not they are both alive AND free.

occurrences.label: If a character tied with homeless spawns was kidnapped or imprisoned but was later released, the homeless spawns tied with said character will all come back to effect. This appears to be intended as it likely accounts for successful rescue operations intended to bring their leader back alive[14], [Town Overrides](/town-overrides) may also switch in certain cases[15], in some cases it is even _necessary_ for the person needed to be initially killed/imprisoned to achieve the override to be _later released_ for the override to persist[16].

findings.finding: The overview generalizes death/imprisonment, Okay predicates, release reversals and the meaning of Prosperous override names.
findings.proposedResolution: Check the exact state predicates, override priority and reentry behavior against the sixteen retained notes; preserve explicit Dust King and Hive Queen exceptions.
findings.uncertainty: A label such as Prosperous is not a measured welfare value, and the overview must not erase character-specific exceptions.

occurrences.label: Generally speaking, it doesn't matter whether you Imprison or Kill a faction leader, the results will remain the same except in a few cases[1][2]. When certain condition states that it requires a person to be dead, imprisoning said character will also work. Conversely, if a condition states that it requires a person to be alive, it means that they should be alive AND free (not imprisoned). If (in [FCS](/forgotten-construction-set)) a condition checks whether or not a person is "Okay", it means whether or not they are both alive AND free.

occurrences.label: If a character tied with homeless spawns was kidnapped or imprisoned but was later released, the homeless spawns tied with said character will all come back to effect. This appears to be intended as it likely accounts for successful rescue operations intended to bring their leader back alive[14], [Town Overrides](/town-overrides) may also switch in certain cases[15], in some cases it is even _necessary_ for the person needed to be initially killed/imprisoned to achieve the override to be _later released_ for the override to persist[16].

occurrences.label: -   Despite popular misconception, many of the overrides that are labelled "Prosperous" in the [FCS](/forgotten-construction-set) does not necessarily mean that the town/city/village in question is more prosperous than it was before and may even be at a worse condition (e.g. more buildings destroyed or more malnourished individuals). Rather, it is considered a "Prosperous" override because when compared to all the other overrides for said area, the override in question is the best one it could achieve.

occurrences.label: Because of how rare your chance of losing limbs is in usual combat[1][2], one way to intentionally lose limbs is to allow wounds to deteriorate on their own and set the limb severing frequency to "frequent"[3], the other way to lose limbs is through the use of the [Peeler Machine](/peeler-machine) or a Fogpole.

occurrences.label: What quality a crafted limb will be is determined by the crafter's [Robotics](/robotics) skill. It's the same skill that is trained by using repair kits and by crafting any components at the Robotics Bench. There is also an element of chance, and the quality can suffer when the crafter is not physically well or working in low light conditions. Unlike a weapon or armor smith, a robotics crafter can attain a skill level at which all products will be max quality. The better limbs require a somewhat complicated crafting procedure when constructed from raw materials. Players crafting in a bought house may simply opt to buy the [Robotics Components](/robotics-components), greatly reducing the fuss.

occurrences.label: NOTE: There is an intentional mechanic from the developers that makes characters with the Diplomat tag "immune" to crossbows. Attempting to shoot units who have a Diplomatic status will usually result in your character aiming at someone else entirely. It is possible to have your marksmen target sometimes glitching and instead hitting an invisible target behind the Diplomat you set to attack. Despite the immunity, your marksmen can have a chance of 'accidentally' hitting the Diplomatic character in front of the unit you are aiming at. On occasion (Sometimes after stealing something from them, assassination attempt etc...) you will be able to shoot to Diplomatic targets with a Crossbow.

occurrences.label: The Eagle's Cross has the longest range and highest accuracy of any bow in the game, shooting farther than even [harpoon turrets](/harpoon-turret), giving it the ability to snipe enemies from extreme ranges in the hands of a skilled marksman. Furthermore, the long range allows for many training opportunities: marksmen can safely rain down bolts upon distant leviathans, or onto denizens of a [cannibal village](/cannibal-village) from the safety of a [watchtower](/watchtower) placed on the outskirts, for example. Furthermore, the Eagle's Cross has a higher bolt velocity, which further increases the hit probability, as it makes it less likely the enemy will deviate from the expected trajectory in the time it takes for the bolt to reach its target.

occurrences.label: It has the same stats (except for dodge mult, that is 0.1 lower) and model as the regular [Samurai Armour](/samurai-armour) but has the [United Cities](/united-cities) emblem on the chest additionally. It cannot be crafted or bought. Wearing one will trigger the [Disguise](/disguise) system. The faction uniform tag can be removed by knocking out a recruitable character (Or an imprisoned one like Agnu in Tower of Abuse or Cat in Dust Kings Tower) and equipping the armour on the unit. When recruited the faction uniform tag will be removed.

occurrences.label: Stolen armour can be [dyed](/colour-scheme) resulting in a different colour scheme than the original. In order to do so a stolen or looted Empire Samurai Armour has to be sold to a vendor to clear it's colour scheme. After which the blank armour can be bought/stolen back and coloured in the usual way. Another way to clear the stolen tag is to place the armour into an [Item Furnace](/item-furnace) or a Crossbow Locker. [Samurai Gate Sergeants](/samurai-gate-sergeant) are a good "source" of specialist (10% chance of MW) quality armour. For guaranteed Masterwork quality Empire Samurai Armour, you can loot _[empire noble guard---](/sandas-noble-guard) found in Bark._

Noble world problems."

occurrences.label: Players can craft robotic limbs on a [Skeleton Limb Bench](/skeleton-limb-bench) and needed components on a [Robotics Bench](/robotics-bench). Unlike with weapon and armor, there are no [Blueprints](/blueprints) for limbs. New crafting options are unlocked by doing research in the [Crafting Tech](/crafting-tech) tree instead. Economy limb research becomes available at tech level 4, Skeleton limbs at tech level 5 and the rest at tech level 6. All robotic limbs are craftable except for the Steady and Thief's arms.
occurrences.literal: Players can craft robotic limbs on a [Skeleton Limb Bench](/skeleton-limb-bench) and needed components on a [Robotics Bench](/robotics-bench). Unlike with weapon and armor, there are no [Blueprints](/blueprints) for limbs. New crafting options are unlocked by doing research in the [Crafting Tech](/crafting-tech) tree instead. Economy limb research becomes available at tech level 4, Skeleton limbs at tech level 5 and the rest at tech level 6. All robotic limbs are craftable except for the Steady and Thief's arms.

occurrences.label: What quality a crafted limb will be is determined by the crafter's [Robotics](/robotics) skill. It's the same skill that is trained by using repair kits and by crafting any components at the Robotics Bench. There is also an element of chance, and the quality can suffer when the crafter is not physically well or working in low light conditions. Unlike a weapon or armor smith, a robotics crafter can attain a skill level at which all products will be max quality. The better limbs require a somewhat complicated crafting procedure when constructed from raw materials. Players crafting in a bought house may simply opt to buy the [Robotics Components](/robotics-components), greatly reducing the fuss.

occurrences.label: **Crab Helmet** is a Heavy Armour that is equipped in the Headgear slot. It is the headgear with the highest blunt resistance. Aside from the races that cannot wear helmets, it additionally cannot be worn by [Hive Worker Drones](/hive-worker-drone) and their [southern](/southern-hive-worker-drone) and [deadhive](/deadhive-worker) cousins. occurrences.label: **Advanced Splint Kits** are [medical](/medical-items) [items](/items) used to improve functionality of injured limbs. Once applied, they help limping characters run normally, except in most extreme cases of limb damage. Players can learn how to craft this item by researching [Advanced Splints](/advanced-splints-tech). After researching, these kits can be crafted on a [Medical Workbench](/medical-workbench) or procured from the NPCs that carry them for personal use - [Wandering Assassins](/wandering-assassin), [Holy Lord Phoenix](/holy-lord-phoenix), [Doctors](/doctor) and [Surgeons](/surgeon).
