occurrences.label: **Blueprints** are used to unlock various [technologies](/technology) as opposed to learning them at a [Research Bench](/research-bench). Many technologies, specifically different types of weapons and armour, cannot be researched normally and need to be learned through blueprints. The trade-off to the new system is that while research times for these technologies are instantaneous the blueprints need to be hunted down, as they are spread out across the world among the various [factions](/factions).

occurrences.label: [Armour](/armour) is clothing which provides armour protection in battle. Heavier armour provides more protection, however it also detracts from other [Statistics](/statistics), such as run speed and stealth. Armour can be purchased from stores, stolen, or found in ancient locations such as [Lost Armouries](/lost-armoury) and [Ancient Labs](/ancient-labs). After some researching, armour can be created at a [Leather Armour Crafting Bench](/leather-armour-crafting-bench), [Chain Armour Crafting Bench](/chain-armour-crafting-bench), or [Heavy Armour Smithy](/heavy-armour-smithy). The quality of [Homemade](/homemade) armour is exclusively dependent on the character's [Armour Smith](/armour-smith) level.
occurrences.literal: [Armour](/armour) is clothing which provides armour protection in battle. Heavier armour provides more protection, however it also detracts from other [Statistics](/statistics), such as run speed and stealth. Armour can be purchased from stores, stolen, or found in ancient locations such as [Lost Armouries](/lost-armoury) and [Ancient Labs](/ancient-labs). After some researching, armour can be created at a [Leather Armour Crafting Bench](/leather-armour-crafting-bench), [Chain Armour Crafting Bench](/chain-armour-crafting-bench), or [Heavy Armour Smithy](/heavy-armour-smithy). The quality of [Homemade](/homemade) armour is exclusively dependent on the character's [Armour Smith](/armour-smith) level.

occurrences.label: [Clothing](/clothing), items which are primarily made of [cloth](/fabrics), provide almost no armour protection. However, they can be helpful for protection from [Weather Effects](/weather-effects). Some clothing items may boost a character's [Martial Arts](/martial-arts) stat or provide protection for their fists. After researching the technology, clothing can be created with the [Clothing Bench](/clothing-bench).

After researching the technology, clothing can be created with the [Clothing Bench](/clothing-bench).

occurrences.label: Weapons and their blueprints can be purchased from [Weapons Shops](/weapons-shops). After researching the technology, weapons can be created at a [Weapon Smithing Bench](/weapon-smithing-bench). The quality of [Homemade](/homemade) weapons is determined by the grades researched, the bench used and the [Weapon Smith](/weapon-smith-skill) level of the character creating them.

occurrences.label: **Trade Goods** are items generally meant for trading, crafting or other uses depending on the item. They buy and sell for their full value unlike most other items, which tend to sell for a much lower value, and are often either ingredients or craftable themselves. [Stolen](/thievery) trade goods, however, will sell for half the price, like most other items. The value at any given town is randomized from town to town to allow for players to make profit via trading between them, though the value is still restricted to +/- 30% from the base value. Some towns also have an additional modifier to specific goods to make them worth more or less there.

occurrences.label: NOTE: There is an intentional mechanic from the developers that makes characters with the Diplomat tag "immune" to crossbows. Attempting to shoot units who have a Diplomatic status will usually result in your character aiming at someone else entirely. It is possible to have your marksmen target sometimes glitching and instead hitting an invisible target behind the Diplomat you set to attack. Despite the immunity, your marksmen can have a chance of 'accidentally' hitting the Diplomatic character in front of the unit you are aiming at. On occasion (Sometimes after stealing something from them, assassination attempt etc...) you will be able to shoot to Diplomatic targets with a Crossbow.

occurrences.label: - The [Crossbows skill](/statistics) itself is a value of 0 to 100[1], multiplied by any equipment Crossbows effect ratios (such as from Ninja Rags). The skill applies to accuracy deviation and reload time. The effects from armour/robotics are multiplicative; that is, 1.1x Crossbows effect from Ninja Rags and 1.25x Crossbows effect from a Steady Arm is 1.375x total (1.1\*1.25, or a 37.5% bonus) rather than a 1.35x total (1.1+1.25, or a 35% bonus). Crossbows effect multipliers also apply to the Precision Shooting skill.

occurrences.label: - **Reload time** - The minimum and maximum time it takes to reload a Crossbow. Your actual reload speed is determined by a ratio of the sum your Crossbows skill and Dexterity compared to the maximum of 200 total. Unlike with accuracy deviation, for the purpose of reload time, this maxes out at 100 for each stat. Going over 100 for either stat via prosthetics or equipment bonuses confers no extra benefit (for example, having 120 Crossbows skill and 50 Dexterity only counts as 150 total). _Lowering reload time is the only way to increase DPS, which means the Crossbows skill and Dexterity are the only factors that contribute to DPS gains for a given type and quality of crossbow._[1]

occurrences.label: Whenever a character is missing any natural limbs, the 'Limbs' button in the inventory window becomes usable and prosthetics can be installed the same way weapons and armor are equipped. (Once installed, robot limbs no longer count toward [Encumbrance](/encumbrance)). All characters, including [Skeletons](/skeleton), need to lose their natural limbs through trauma before Robot Limbs can be used. When a limb is lost a character receives 0.2 bleeding and 0.002 "steady bleeding" for every cut damage (and negative bandaged health) on the limb. Steady bleeding will not stop until bandaged or it can be stopped instantly by putting a robotic limb in the place of the lost limb. Animals cannot lose limbs or use prosthetics.

occurrences.label: Robot Limbs need to be maintained in the same way Skeletons maintain themselves, which is notably expensive. Cut damage can be fixed on the spot with a [Robotics Repair Kit](/robotics-repair-kit). The "wear and tear damage" that builds up over time (4% of total damage taken is applied as wear damage) and decreases the max health of a limb can be fixed using a [Skeleton Repair Bed](/skeleton-repair-bed). These Repair Beds can be typically found in locations which sell limbs and usually require payment the same way a bar bed does (albeit significantly more expensive).

occurrences.label: Crossbows can do a decent amount of damage to a single target and cause significant bleeding. It is important to note that the size of the target (and its hitbox) plays an important role in the accuracy of crossbows. As such, large animals are easier to hit than humanoids, but so also it's more difficult to hit small targets like spiders. Players should to be cautious using crossbow characters and especially positioning them with particular care during fights, it's not rare for high-powered crossbows to kill weaker enemies, _**and so too allies succumb to friendly fire**_, outright and permanently.

occurrences.label: The usefulness of blunt weapons is heavily questioned by many players. Blunt weapons offer less or the same amount of total damage as light weapons (Sabres, Polearms, Katanas) while demanding equally (if not more) strength as most [Hackers](/hackers), sometimes even [Heavy Weapons](/heavy-weapons) - and not providing extra range or other benefits (the Clubs have some bonuses, but those are inferior to ones given by most hackers). However, their strength requirements combined with the popularity of Clubs can make them **a potential steppingstone for early strength training**. It is also worth noting that **the majority of armours have a lower resistance for blunt than cut damage**, sometimes quite significantly.

occurrences.label: The **Falling Sun**, like the other [Heavy Weapons](/heavy-weapons-class), has an extremely high damage potential, sometimes doing enough damage to outright kill an opponent in one hit. The Falling Sun is the lightest of the Heavy Weapons. As it has a lower blunt damage amount, it requires less strength to be able to use it effectively. An experienced user is someone to be feared.

occurrences.label: **Heavy Jittes**, along with their smaller counterpart the [Jitte](/jitte), are [Blunt weapons](/blunt-weapons) that inflict [stun damage](/stun-damage) (blunt) and extremely minor cut damage/blood loss. As Dexterity experience gained is based off the cut damage of a weapon, using either of the two variants will reward no Dexterity at all. Due to their lack of any serious cut damage this makes them somewhat useful for subduing bandit leaders and other [bounties](/bounty) without running the risk of them dying due to wound degeneration. Please note that KO time is almost entirely based on blood loss and cut damage received, stun damage only adds time when hit under 0 health in a bodypart so characters knocked out with a Heavy Jitte may get up very quickly before you can pick them up.

occurrences.label: **Heavy Weapons** weigh more than most weapons and use a move set more centered around fighting large groups of units. Heavy weapons require brute force and deal heavy blunt [damage](/damage). A heavy weapon will typically inflict more damage than other weapons but if you lack the strength to use them you will attack and block much slower. Due to their reach paired with their move set, when surrounded heavy weapons are very useful for hitting multiple enemies with each swing.

occurrences.label: Like all weapons, attack speed, with heavy weapons is determined by a combination of having enough [Strength](/strength) to use it effectively, [Dexterity](/dexterity), as well as [Melee Attack](/melee-attack). Block speed is determined by a combination of having enough Strength to use it effectively, Dexterity, as well as [Melee Defense](/melee-defense). The base attack speed is 0.765, every level in Dexterity will increase this by 0.00228, and 0.00152 for attack. Strength comes into play in the required strength level of the weapon, if below its required level your combat speed will be penalized (up to -47.5% at 20 levels or more below). Strength above the required level does not affect speed at all, beyond acting as a buffer for injuries penalizing your strength. The strength requirement to use a weapon is the blunt damage multiplied by 40[1].

occurrences.label: **Katanas** are a class of [weapons](/weapons) that specialize in cutting damage. They are a very commonly found weapon type, and their low weight makes them easy for beginners to use.
occurrences.literal: **Katanas** are a class of [weapons](/weapons) that specialize in cutting damage. They are a very commonly found weapon type, and their low weight makes them easy for beginners to use.

occurrences.label: Katanas are offensive weapons, featuring attack bonuses and defense penalties, as well as a high blood loss multiplier. A major characteristic of Katanas are big penalties for armour penetration and robot damage, making them a poor choice for the latter stages of the game. However, they are quite useful against early-game enemies, who are predominantly humans in little to no armor.
occurrences.literal: Katanas are offensive weapons, featuring attack bonuses and defense penalties, as well as a high blood loss multiplier. A major characteristic of Katanas are big penalties for armour penetration and robot damage, making them a poor choice for the latter stages of the game. However, they are quite useful against early-game enemies, who are predominantly humans in little to no armor.

occurrences.label: They feature a two-hit combo attack (called Downward Combo) that makes them particularly useful when fighting animals or singular weak opponents but leaves their wielder vulnerable to getting hit in battles with multiple foes. The combo attack is the only weapon animation[1] which has less than 100 power (100% of the weapon's damage). It makes up for this by attacking twice: the power of the first strike is 80 and the second one is 60. Unfortunately, though, Downward Combo is usually too slow_\[clarify\]_ to land the second hit on an opponent if they were staggered by another attack. This leads to overall less damage over time when compared to weapon types like [Sabres](/sabres) or [Polearms](/polearms)[2].

occurrences.label: A **Nodachi** is a [Katana Class](/katanas) weapon. Heavier, with increased range and damage compared to most katanas at the expense of indoor penalties. It is very widely used, including by many of the more elite samurai of the [United Cities](/united-cities). It has the second lowest Armour Penetration penalty of the Katanas (Ninja blade has -20% as well but it is Ninja blade so...) making it decent (Katana wise) for taking on armoured foes. Due to the reduced Defense and indoor penalty, a Rusted Junk version can be used to level Defense up extremely fast inside of a building.

occurrences.label: **Polearms** are a class of weapon that excels at speed and reach. Most have bonus damage against animals. [Polearm](/polearm) and [Heavy Polearm](/heavy-polearm) are notably the only weapons which provide an armour penetration bonus without having high strength requirements[1].
occurrences.literal: **Polearms** are a class of weapon that excels at speed and reach. Most have bonus damage against animals. [Polearm](/polearm) and [Heavy Polearm](/heavy-polearm) are notably the only weapons which provide an armour penetration bonus without having high strength requirements[1].

occurrences.label: All Polearms have moderate attack bonuses and indoor penalties. Polearms also have the second highest blood loss multipliers out of all weapon classes (bested only by Katanas, which also have significant downsides).
occurrences.literal: All Polearms have moderate attack bonuses and indoor penalties. Polearms also have the second highest blood loss multipliers out of all weapon classes (bested only by Katanas, which also have significant downsides).

occurrences.label: They are an excellent choice for low-skilled characters, as they have a very low strength requirement and a move set similar to [Katanas](/katanas) and [Sabres](/sabres) while providing similar damage and much higher range. In particular, [Polearm](/polearm) not only has the highest animal damage multiplier but also a high armour penetration. However, [Heavy Polearm](/heavy-polearm) has a significantly lower (sic!) strength requirement and provides higher base damage, possibly making it a better option for general use.

occurrences.label: Combat is a primary part of Kenshi, and all combat except for martial arts is done with weapons. Weapons are [items](/items) that are split into multiple categories, each dealing different types and amounts of damage. [Armour](/armour) is designed to reduce damage and can be slightly penetrated by using certain weapons. Weapons can be looted, purchased from a [Weapons Trader](/weapons-trader), or crafted by the player.

occurrences.label: caption: "A rare, extreme long-range weapon for snipers.  It's possible to do a lot of damage with one of these before an enemy even realises what is happening to them.  Takes skill to use effectively, and not much use at short range."
occurrences.literal: caption: "A rare, extreme long-range weapon for snipers.  It's possible to do a lot of damage with one of these before an enemy even realises what is happening to them.  Takes skill to use effectively, and not much use at short range."

occurrences.label: **Eagle's Cross** is a [Crossbow](/crossbow-class) with farthest range and highest damage of any ranged weapon. It can be dangerous in the hands of an unskilled shooter; a single friendly-fire shot could kill any low-toughness allies.
occurrences.literal: **Eagle's Cross** is a [Crossbow](/crossbow-class) with farthest range and highest damage of any ranged weapon. It can be dangerous in the hands of an unskilled shooter; a single friendly-fire shot could kill any low-toughness allies.

occurrences.label: It is the only Crossbow which requires [Long Bolts](/bolts-longs) which only hold 10 shots and weigh 2kg each stack. On long adventures a smaller crossbow may be more suitable due to this. The primary use for an Eagle's Cross is to eliminate targets from far distances and to deal with opponents who wear armour with high harpoon resistance.
occurrences.literal: It is the only Crossbow which requires [Long Bolts](/bolts-longs) which only hold 10 shots and weigh 2kg each stack. On long adventures a smaller crossbow may be more suitable due to this. The primary use for an Eagle's Cross is to eliminate targets from far distances and to deal with opponents who wear armour with high harpoon resistance.

occurrences.label: The Eagle's Cross does more damage per shot, making it a superior choice against armoured opponents, as it will overcome the target's harpoon resistance, leading to greater damage. Furthermore, a masterwork-quality bow is capable of one-shotting many enemies, including human enemies up to a moderate degrees of toughness, with light armour. If including height advantage, the Eagle's Cross is capable of doing over 200 damage to low-toughness enemies, one-shotting some [robots](/robots) when shooting from a high cliff, for example. In contrast, the Oldworld Bow MkII is generally limited to one-shotting only weak enemies with no armour.
occurrences.literal: The Eagle's Cross does more damage per shot, making it a superior choice against armoured opponents, as it will overcome the target's harpoon resistance, leading to greater damage. Furthermore, a masterwork-quality bow is capable of one-shotting many enemies, including human enemies up to a moderate degrees of toughness, with light armour. If including height advantage, the Eagle's Cross is capable of doing over 200 damage to low-toughness enemies, one-shotting some [robots](/robots) when shooting from a high cliff, for example. In contrast, the Oldworld Bow MkII is generally limited to one-shotting only weak enemies with no armour.

occurrences.label: At low crossbow and dexterity levels, the Oldworld Bow MkII has only a slightly better rate of fire, and a significantly inferior damage output than the Eagle's Cross: as noted in game, the Oldworld Bow MkII can be difficult for beginners to reload; this is reflected in-game by its reload time scaling more on user skill than other bows; an Eagle's Cross will double its rate of fire going from minimum to maximum crossbow skill and dexterity, while a Oldworld Bow MkII has its rate of fire increase by 2.87 times.
occurrences.literal: At low crossbow and dexterity levels, the Oldworld Bow MkII has only a slightly better rate of fire, and a significantly inferior damage output than the Eagle's Cross: as noted in game, the Oldworld Bow MkII can be difficult for beginners to reload; this is reflected in-game by its reload time scaling more on user skill than other bows; an Eagle's Cross will double its rate of fire going from minimum to maximum crossbow skill and dexterity, while a Oldworld Bow MkII has its rate of fire increase by 2.87 times.

occurrences.label: However, at very high skill levels, the Oldworld Bow MkII has superior damage output (against unarmoured foes) and a very rapid rate of fire. The Oldworld Bow reaches damage-per-second parity with the Eagle's Cross at about 75 crossbow skill and dexterity, while with the aforementioned skills at 100 (which can be more practically achieved with with the aid of buffs from [Robot Limbs](/robot-limbs) or outfits such as the [Assassin's Rags](/assassins-rags)), the Oldworld Bow MkII has a 16% greater damage per second.
occurrences.literal: However, at very high skill levels, the Oldworld Bow MkII has superior damage output (against unarmoured foes) and a very rapid rate of fire. The Oldworld Bow reaches damage-per-second parity with the Eagle's Cross at about 75 crossbow skill and dexterity, while with the aforementioned skills at 100 (which can be more practically achieved with with the aid of buffs from [Robot Limbs](/robot-limbs) or outfits such as the [Assassin's Rags](/assassins-rags)), the Oldworld Bow MkII has a 16% greater damage per second.

occurrences.label: Per point of damage, assuming the Eagle's Cross does 50% more damage per bolt, which is roughly accurate (it depends on the quality level).
occurrences.literal: Per point of damage, assuming the Eagle's Cross does 50% more damage per bolt, which is roughly accurate (it depends on the quality level).

occurrences.label: While the Eagle's Cross's higher damage is generally an advantage, it is a detriment in friendly-fire situations. While fighters in heavy armour can generally shrug off many accidental hits from the Oldworld Bow MkII, friendly fire from the Eagle's Cross can sometimes prove catastrophic — knocking out, maiming or even outright killing allies in a single shot. If one wants to provide supporting fire to melee fighters, with the Eagle's Cross, it is recommended to only use high-toughness melee fighters with good quality — and in particular, high coverage — armours, such as [Crab Armour](/crab-armour) with underlying [Chainmail](/chainmail) armour. Players should also consider the effect that height advantage may have on any friendly-fire damage.
occurrences.literal: While the Eagle's Cross's higher damage is generally an advantage, it is a detriment in friendly-fire situations. While fighters in heavy armour can generally shrug off many accidental hits from the Oldworld Bow MkII, friendly fire from the Eagle's Cross can sometimes prove catastrophic — knocking out, maiming or even outright killing allies in a single shot. If one wants to provide supporting fire to melee fighters, with the Eagle's Cross, it is recommended to only use high-toughness melee fighters with good quality — and in particular, high coverage — armours, such as [Crab Armour](/crab-armour) with underlying [Chainmail](/chainmail) armour. Players should also consider the effect that height advantage may have on any friendly-fire damage.

occurrences.label: The Eagle's Cross does more damage per shot, making it a superior choice against armoured opponents, as it will overcome the target's harpoon resistance, leading to greater damage. Furthermore, a masterwork-quality bow is capable of one-shotting many enemies, including human enemies up to a moderate degrees of toughness, with light armour. If including height advantage, the Eagle's Cross is capable of doing over 200 damage to low-toughness enemies, one-shotting some [robots](/robots) when shooting from a high cliff, for example. In contrast, the Oldworld Bow MkII is generally limited to one-shotting only weak enemies with no armour.

occurrences.label: However, at very high skill levels, the Oldworld Bow MkII has superior damage output (against unarmoured foes) and a very rapid rate of fire. occurrences.label: **Crab Helmet** is a Heavy Armour that is equipped in the Headgear slot. It is the headgear with the highest blunt resistance. Aside from the races that cannot wear helmets, it additionally cannot be worn by [Hive Worker Drones](/hive-worker-drone) and their [southern](/southern-hive-worker-drone) and [deadhive](/deadhive-worker) cousins. It can be crafted once a blueprint is purchased from the [Crab Raiders](/crab-raiders) and is part of a Crab Armour "set", together with [Crab Armour](/crab-armour) (body), [Crab Trousers](/crab-trousers) and [Crab Shoes](/crab-shoes).

occurrences.label: Mercenary Leather Armour is built from several different pieces of leather covering most of the front chest, part of the stomach, with several leather pads strapped on the arms and hands. Currently the in-game model looks very similar to [Mercenary Plate](/mercenary-plate) minus the shoulder guards, giving less coverage to the arms compared to their plated counterpart.
occurrences.literal: Mercenary Leather Armour is built from several different pieces of leather covering most of the front chest, part of the stomach, with several leather pads strapped on the arms and hands. Currently the in-game model looks very similar to [Mercenary Plate](/mercenary-plate) minus the shoulder guards, giving less coverage to the arms compared to their plated counterpart.

occurrences.label: Compared with [Conscript Leather Armour](/conscript-leather-armour), which on appearance should be a white version of **Mercenary Leather Armour,** they do offer different protection against blunt and cut resistance with the amount of difference being variable, depending on the grade. Harpoon resistance is the same or just one point in favour of the Mercenary version. The coverage and the skill penalties are always the same. The value of Mercenary armour is always higher than Conscript.
occurrences.literal: Compared with [Conscript Leather Armour](/conscript-leather-armour), which on appearance should be a white version of **Mercenary Leather Armour,** they do offer different protection against blunt and cut resistance with the amount of difference being variable, depending on the grade. Harpoon resistance is the same or just one point in favour of the Mercenary version. The coverage and the skill penalties are always the same. The value of Mercenary armour is always higher than Conscript.

occurrences.label: Starting the comparison at **prototype** grade, Conscript does not provide any protection all, thus is Mercenary the better choice. When quality is improved to **shoddy** grade, the Mercenary armour outclasses the counterpart with 2%, 4% more blunt and cut resistance and 1 point in harpoon resistance. At **Standard** grade, the Conscript version offers 2% more blunt resistance, at the expense of 1 point harpoon resistance, making the armour slightly better than the Mercenary version.
occurrences.literal: Starting the comparison at **prototype** grade, Conscript does not provide any protection all, thus is Mercenary the better choice. When quality is improved to **shoddy** grade, the Mercenary armour outclasses the counterpart with 2%, 4% more blunt and cut resistance and 1 point in harpoon resistance. At **Standard** grade, the Conscript version offers 2% more blunt resistance, at the expense of 1 point harpoon resistance, making the armour slightly better than the Mercenary version.

occurrences.label: Compared to **high** quality, they offer the same protection, expect harpoon resistance. From **Specialist** quality onwards, Conscript offers more blunt resistance, while Mercenary armour offers more cut resistance. The difference in protection are 2% for blunt and 4% cutting. At **Masterwork**, these differences are 4% and 5% respectively.
occurrences.literal: Compared to **high** quality, they offer the same protection, expect harpoon resistance. From **Specialist** quality onwards, Conscript offers more blunt resistance, while Mercenary armour offers more cut resistance. The difference in protection are 2% for blunt and 4% cutting. At **Masterwork**, these differences are 4% and 5% respectively.

occurrences.label: As conclusion, Mercenary is better at low qualities, near equal at standard and high quality and offers more cutting resistance at specialist and masterwork, but at these grades, offers less blunt protection compared to Conscript.
occurrences.literal: As conclusion, Mercenary is better at low qualities, near equal at standard and high quality and offers more cutting resistance at specialist and masterwork, but at these grades, offers less blunt protection compared to Conscript.

occurrences.label: As noted in-game, the Mercenary Plate is a versatile medium-heavy armour, trading some defence for increased offensive capabilities, with only a -4 penalty to attack skill, and lacking the .85 damage modifier of the [Samurai Armour](/samurai-armour), for example. In terms of protection, it gives roughly one third less protection against cut damage, although the blunt damage protection is almost on par, making it a good choice against foes using mainly blunt damage, especially against enemies who have stats roughly on parity with the player and against whom the effect of stat debuffs are more significant.
occurrences.literal: As noted in-game, the Mercenary Plate is a versatile medium-heavy armour, trading some defence for increased offensive capabilities, with only a -4 penalty to attack skill, and lacking the .85 damage modifier of the [Samurai Armour](/samurai-armour), for example. In terms of protection, it gives roughly one third less protection against cut damage, although the blunt damage protection is almost on par, making it a good choice against foes using mainly blunt damage, especially against enemies who have stats roughly on parity with the player and against whom the effect of stat debuffs are more significant.

occurrences.label: A player may consider using the Mercenary Plate with [Leather Turtleneck](/leather-turtleneck) or [Martial Artist Bindings](/martial-artist-bindings) if he wants to maintain a dextrous medium-heavy fighter. The [Samurai Legplates](/samurai-legplates) also pair well with the Mercenary Plate, due to having 50% stomach coverage, helping to cover the gap in the Mercenary Plate's protection.

occurrences.label: The **Plate Jacket** is a Medium Armour that is equipped in the Body Armour slot. It can be normally found sold in [Mongrel](/mongrel), [United Cities](/united-cities), [Shek](/shek-kingdom), and [Tech Hunter](/tech-hunters) armour shops. It is one of the only body armours that covers 100% of the entire upper body. It is the worst of the three plate jackets, suffering from the Stealth and Assassination penalties that the black variant is free of, while also sharing the same inferior Dexterity penalty compared to the white variant. It also suffers from a 1% worse Cut Resistance across its Specialist and Masterwork grades.

occurrences.label: **Advanced Splint Kits** are [medical](/medical-items) [items](/items) used to improve functionality of injured limbs. occurrences.label: Characters which are Skeletons or have robot limbs will need Skeleton Repair Kits to heal their robotic body parts. occurrences.label: Splint Kits are used to temporarily give HP to significantly damaged organic limbs. If a limb falls below 50 health, a Splint Kit can be used to fix it. Splinting can only be used if the unit has bandaged health on them. (Having 0 health due to 100 stun damage will not allow you to splint) The splint kit currently comes in two different sizes. You can splint up to your field medic skill, with a cap of the quality + 1. (Advanced capping at 51 rigged health, normal kit 26)

occurrences.label: First Aid, Splint and Skeleton Repair Kits possess a quality modifier, which must be met by your [Field Medic](/field-medic) or [Robotics](/robotics) skills to be effectively used. Having a higher skill also reduces the speed in which the Kit will be used up. Lack of lighting will only reduce the robotics skill, but injuries reduce both field medic and robotics. The reduction is -0.45% skill for every 1% max hp in damage received on a character's head. To give an example, a Greenlander with 80 damage done to their head will have -36% Field Medic/Robotics (0.45x80).

occurrences.literal: ## [Faction uniforms](/faction-uniform)

occurrences.label: A Faction Uniform is armour that some [Factions](/factions) members may wear. An **armour** is considered a Faction Uniform if the clothing is tagged as being a uniform of a set faction. Player Characters wearing Faction Uniforms will be considered "[in Disguise](/disguise)" and may be arrested by police for [Uniform Theft](/bounty).
occurrences.literal: A Faction Uniform is armour that some [Factions](/factions) members may wear. An **armour** is considered a Faction Uniform if the clothing is tagged as being a uniform of a set faction. Player Characters wearing Faction Uniforms will be considered "[in Disguise](/disguise)" and may be arrested by police for [Uniform Theft](/bounty).

occurrences.label: Your characters may be allowed to wear a Faction Uniform if you are allied with that particular faction. Note that factions which are hostile to the faction you are wearing the uniform of may also attack you, mistaking you for their enemy.
occurrences.literal: Your characters may be allowed to wear a Faction Uniform if you are allied with that particular faction. Note that factions which are hostile to the faction you are wearing the uniform of may also attack you, mistaking you for their enemy.

occurrences.label: You can remove a faction uniform by knocking out (Assassination) a recruitable character like a Drifter and making them wear the uniform. They MUST be wearing it. After that wait for them to wake back up and recruit them. This will remove the Faction Uniform tag. (If the character is hostile with you as you were caught knocking them out, wait around 5 game hours and they should return to neutral or leave and come back later.)

occurrences.label: It has the same stats (except for dodge mult, that is 0.1 lower) and model as the regular [Samurai Armour](/samurai-armour) but has the [United Cities](/united-cities) emblem on the chest additionally. It cannot be crafted or bought. Wearing one will trigger the [Disguise](/disguise) system. The faction uniform tag can be removed by knocking out a recruitable character (Or an imprisoned one like Agnu in Tower of Abuse or Cat in Dust Kings Tower) and equipping the armour on the unit. When recruited the faction uniform tag will be removed.

occurrences.label: Stolen armour can be [dyed](/colour-scheme) resulting in a different colour scheme than the original. In order to do so a stolen or looted Empire Samurai Armour has to be sold to a vendor to clear it's colour scheme. After which the blank armour can be bought/stolen back and coloured in the usual way. Another way to clear the stolen tag is to place the armour into an [Item Furnace](/item-furnace) or a Crossbow Locker. [Samurai Gate Sergeants](/samurai-gate-sergeant) are a good "source" of specialist (10% chance of MW) quality armour. For guaranteed Masterwork quality Empire Samurai Armour, you can loot _[empire noble guard---](/sandas-noble-guard) found in Bark._

occurrences.label: **Food** consists of all the items in Kenshi which fill your [hunger](/guide-to-health#hunger) bar. A character's hunger bar is filled by 1 for every nutrition charge used. They automatically consume some food when their hunger gets below 250, unless the only types of food they have are edible ingredients. In that case, they will not eat them until the hunger level gets below 200.
occurrences.literal: **Food** consists of all the items in Kenshi which fill your [hunger](/guide-to-health#hunger) bar. A character's hunger bar is filled by 1 for every nutrition charge used. They automatically consume some food when their hunger gets below 250, unless the only types of food they have are edible ingredients. In that case, they will not eat them until the hunger level gets below 200.

occurrences.label: Characters can eat any food in their own or their squad member's inventories, including that in their backpack. After eating, the hunger bar slowly fills up over time. Characters of different [Races](/races) have different rates at which their hunger drains, which is also dependent on any action that a character is doing, i.e., it will drain more slowly if a character is idle and faster if a character is working.

occurrences.label: Hackers are a relatively uncommon weapon type and rarely show up in shops (with the exception of Long Cleavers, which are commonly sold by Sheks). Low quality Flesh Cleavers can be found on [Cannibals](/cannibals) and [Shrieking Bandits](/shrieking-bandits). [Paladin's Cross](/paladins-cross) is wielded by [Paladins](/paladin), who tend to travel in large groups and have decent stats, making this an unlikely place to get hackers from. [Band of Bones](/band-of-bones) frequently wield Rusted Blade quality Combat Cleavers, making them a good source of hackers in the early game. Various medium-high quality hackers spawn via the [Artifacts](/artifacts) system.

occurrences.label: The Eagle's Cross has the longest range and highest accuracy of any bow in the game, shooting farther than even [harpoon turrets](/harpoon-turret), giving it the ability to snipe enemies from extreme ranges in the hands of a skilled marksman. Furthermore, the long range allows for many training opportunities: marksmen can safely rain down bolts upon distant leviathans, or onto denizens of a [cannibal village](/cannibal-village) from the safety of a [watchtower](/watchtower) placed on the outskirts, for example. Furthermore, the Eagle's Cross has a higher bolt velocity, which further increases the hit probability, as it makes it less likely the enemy will deviate from the expected trajectory in the time it takes for the bolt to reach its target.

Although some especially notorious raiding bands hailed from Hessen, a central state of Germany, the name became generalized as a term for any German Mercenary. Some think of Hessians only as German mercenaries that were hired by British forces during the American Revolutionary War. In reality, Hessen is a county of Germany, nothing more. Hessian cloth, however, is more commonly called burlap.

occurrences.label: What quality a crafted limb will be is determined by the crafter's [Robotics](/robotics) skill. It's the same skill that is trained by using repair kits and by crafting any components at the Robotics Bench. There is also an element of chance, and the quality can suffer when the crafter is not physically well or working in low light conditions. Unlike a weapon or armor smith, a robotics crafter can attain a skill level at which all products will be max quality. The better limbs require a somewhat complicated crafting procedure when constructed from raw materials. Players crafting in a bought house may simply opt to buy the [Robotics Components](/robotics-components), greatly reducing the fuss.

occurrences.label: NOTE: There is an intentional mechanic from the developers that makes characters with the Diplomat tag "immune" to crossbows. Attempting to shoot units who have a Diplomatic status will usually result in your character aiming at someone else entirely. It is possible to have your marksmen target sometimes glitching and instead hitting an invisible target behind the Diplomat you set to attack. Despite the immunity, your marksmen can have a chance of 'accidentally' hitting the Diplomatic character in front of the unit you are aiming at. On occasion (Sometimes after stealing something from them, assassination attempt etc...) you will be able to shoot to Diplomatic targets with a Crossbow.

occurrences.label: Stolen armour can be [dyed](/colour-scheme) resulting in a different colour scheme than the original. In order to do so a stolen or looted Empire Samurai Armour has to be sold to a vendor to clear it's colour scheme. After which the blank armour can be bought/stolen back and coloured in the usual way. Another way to clear the stolen tag is to place the armour into an [Item Furnace](/item-furnace) or a Crossbow Locker. [Samurai Gate Sergeants](/samurai-gate-sergeant) are a good "source" of specialist (10% chance of MW) quality armour. For guaranteed Masterwork quality Empire Samurai Armour, you can loot _[empire noble guard---](/sandas-noble-guard) found in Bark._

occurrences.label: **Medical Items** are items which can be used to heal characters. Medical Items are entirely separate from the trade good [Medical Supplies](/medical-supplies), which has no functional use. First Aid Kits and Splint Kits can be used on all non-skeleton races. Healing large amounts of health takes a lot of time and it is recommended that characters rest in a [Bed](/bed) (8x) or a [Camp Bed](/camp-bed) (4x) to speed it up.

occurrences.label: Characters which are Skeletons or have robot limbs will need Skeleton Repair Kits to heal their robotic body parts. Skeletons and robot limbs regenerate to a slightly lower health after each time they are damaged, but this wear and tear can be repaired with a [Skeleton Repair Bed](/skeleton-repair-bed). Wear damage is a reduction of max health equal to 4% of damage taken. If characters are non-skeleton with robot limbs, their non-robotic body parts will be repaired at a high rate while sleeping on a Repair Bed as well.

occurrences.label: After a character of any race has a limb drop to -100% of the limb's total possible health and (When set to rare) is struck in combat they lose that limb. Skeletons are not exempt from losing limbs in this way. There are settings in the [Options Menu](/options-menu) which can increase or decrease the likelihood of loss of limbs. The options are Never, Rare (Default) and Frequent. When set to Frequent simply dropping to -100% health in the limb will cause it to fall off. You can put a [Robot Limb](/robot-limbs) in the "limb" slot shortly after losing one to stop a LOT of the bleeding.

occurrences.label: First Aid, Splint and Skeleton Repair Kits possess a quality modifier, which must be met by your [Field Medic](/field-medic) or [Robotics](/robotics) skills to be effectively used. Having a higher skill also reduces the speed in which the Kit will be used up. Lack of lighting will only reduce the robotics skill, but injuries reduce both field medic and robotics. The reduction is -0.45% skill for every 1% max hp in damage received on a character's head. To give an example, a Greenlander with 80 damage done to their head will have -36% Field Medic/Robotics (0.45x80).

occurrences.label: **Skeleton Repair Kits** are [medical](/medical-items) [items](/items) used to heal cutting [damage](/damage) on [robotic](/robots) body parts. Players can learn how to craft this item by researching [Robotics](/robotics-tech). After researching, these kits can be crafted on a [Robotics Bench](/robotics-bench). These kits can be stored in [Storage: Robotics](/storage-robotics).

findings.finding: Blunt-weapon guidance differs in how strongly it promises non-lethal capture.
findings.proposedResolution: Compare damage, bleeding and coma conditions and retain differences between advice and guaranteed behavior.
findings.uncertainty: A low bleeding multiplier does not by itself guarantee a living target.
findings.postCutover: Serve the registered article with the imported qualification; keep this investigation open. Conversion is not gameplay verification.

occurrences.label: Because stun (blunt) damage actually [reduces KO time for the most part](/damage), enemies defeated with a blunt weapon will get up very quickly after getting knocked out. A character knocked out with pure stun damage will stand up seconds (if not instantly) after being knocked unconscious (unless put into a recovery coma).
occurrences.literal: Because stun (blunt) damage actually [reduces KO time for the most part](/damage), enemies defeated with a blunt weapon will get up very quickly after getting knocked out. A character knocked out with pure stun damage will stand up seconds (if not instantly) after being knocked unconscious (unless put into a recovery coma).

occurrences.label: A commonly brought up point is that Blunt Weapons are useful for defeating bounties, because it removes the need to bandage them and reduces the chance of them dying (from bleeding and wound degeneration). However, this claim has significant flaws:
occurrences.literal: A commonly brought up point is that Blunt Weapons are useful for defeating bounties, because it removes the need to bandage them and reduces the chance of them dying (from bleeding and wound degeneration). However, this claim has significant flaws:

occurrences.label: -   Killing a bounty before being able to bandage them is already very unlikely unless using an incredibly skilled characters with high damage weapons.
occurrences.literal: -   Killing a bounty before being able to bandage them is already very unlikely unless using an incredibly skilled characters with high damage weapons.

occurrences.label: -   The short KO time can make it harder to actually pick up the bounty in the middle of a fight.
occurrences.literal: -   The short KO time can make it harder to actually pick up the bounty in the middle of a fight.

occurrences.label: -   You have to either do a lot of micromanaging to only attack the bounty with a blunt-wielding character or equip an entire squad with blunt weapons. Crossbows also cannot be used.
occurrences.literal: -   You have to either do a lot of micromanaging to only attack the bounty with a blunt-wielding character or equip an entire squad with blunt weapons. Crossbows also cannot be used.

occurrences.label: -   You will have a harder time trying to defeat the bounty (and their crowd of supporters, which bounties often have) with blunt weapons compared to other weapon classes.
occurrences.literal: -   You will have a harder time trying to defeat the bounty (and their crowd of supporters, which bounties often have) with blunt weapons compared to other weapon classes.

occurrences.label: **Jittes**, along with their larger counterpart the [Heavy Jitte](/heavy-jitte), are [Blunt weapons](/blunt-weapons) that inflict [Stun Damage](/stun-damage) and an extremely minor amount of cut damage/blood loss classifying them as a non-lethal weapon. This allows you to subdue and capture bandit leaders without the risk of them dying from wound degeneration or blood loss.

occurrences.label: **Iron Clubs** are [Blunt class weapons](/blunt-weapons) introduced in update 0.42. With a focus on [Blunt Damage](/stun-damage), they make decent tools for capturing bandits and other criminals for their bounties. Packs of [Escaped Servants](/escaped-servant), [Slave Hunters](/slave-hunters), [Holy Servants](/holy-servant) and [Starving Bandits](/starving-bandits) are known to carry these, often of the rusted variety.

occurrences.label: What quality a crafted limb will be is determined by the crafter's [Robotics](/robotics) skill. It's the same skill that is trained by using repair kits and by crafting any components at the Robotics Bench. There is also an element of chance, and the quality can suffer when the crafter is not physically well or working in low light conditions. Unlike a weapon or armor smith, a robotics crafter can attain a skill level at which all products will be max quality. The better limbs require a somewhat complicated crafting procedure when constructed from raw materials. Players crafting in a bought house may simply opt to buy the [Robotics Components](/robotics-components), greatly reducing the fuss.

occurrences.label: The damage, accuracy, range, projectile speed, reload time are all affected by the quality of the weapon. A low-quality weapon will never reach the best values while the highest quality bows have minimum values much higher than the worst quality versions. Unlike other weapons Crossbows use the same quality as Armour, ranging from Prototype to Masterwork. Contrary to what is listed on a Crossbow's description they all have a Bloodloss value of 2.0x. (As in if a shot would do 100 damage against a Greenlander, then they will instantly lose 40 blood)

occurrences.label: - The [Crossbows skill](/statistics) itself is a value of 0 to 100[1], multiplied by any equipment Crossbows effect ratios (such as from Ninja Rags). The skill applies to accuracy deviation and reload time. The effects from armour/robotics are multiplicative; that is, 1.1x Crossbows effect from Ninja Rags and 1.25x Crossbows effect from a Steady Arm is 1.375x total (1.1\*1.25, or a 37.5% bonus) rather than a 1.35x total (1.1+1.25, or a 35% bonus). Crossbows effect multipliers also apply to the Precision Shooting skill.

occurrences.label: - **Accuracy deviation** - A range of degrees by which a shot can be off-center, it's determined by crossbow type and quality. The deviation is reduced by a percentage equal to the sum of a character's Perception and Crossbows skill, to theoretically no deviation at 200 total. Higher Crossbows skill can substitute for Perception and vice versa.[1]
occurrences.literal: - **Accuracy deviation** - A range of degrees by which a shot can be off-center, it's determined by crossbow type and quality. The deviation is reduced by a percentage equal to the sum of a character's Perception and Crossbows skill, to theoretically no deviation at 200 total. Higher Crossbows skill can substitute for Perception and vice versa.[1]

occurrences.label: - **Reload time** - The minimum and maximum time it takes to reload a Crossbow. Your actual reload speed is determined by a ratio of the sum your Crossbows skill and Dexterity compared to the maximum of 200 total. Unlike with accuracy deviation, for the purpose of reload time, this maxes out at 100 for each stat. Going over 100 for either stat via prosthetics or equipment bonuses confers no extra benefit (for example, having 120 Crossbows skill and 50 Dexterity only counts as 150 total). _Lowering reload time is the only way to increase DPS, which means the Crossbows skill and Dexterity are the only factors that contribute to DPS gains for a given type and quality of crossbow._[1]

occurrences.label: High-quality versions of this weapon are commonly found in the [Scraphouse](/scraphouse). Low to Medium quality versions of this weapon are sometimes found in [Shek](/shek-kingdom), [Mongrel](/mongrel), [Flotsam](/flotsam-ninjas), and [Tech Hunter](/tech-hunters) weapon shops. [Cross](/cross)\-manufactured Falling Sun is found on one [ancient leader](/mad-cat-lon). A Rusted Junk quality version may be found extremely rarely in bars in [The Hub](/the-hub) or [Mourn](/mourn), in shops in the Shek Kingdom, or crafted.

occurrences.label: [Edgewalker](/edgewalkers) and above variants of the weapon are so absurdly heavy that it is impossible for character without robotic limbs to wield them without penalties. Even with robotics, a very high level of strength is needed in order to use the higher quality variants efficiently. The Cross variant requires a character to have 144 STR to use without their combat speed being reduced, which cannot be achieved without [Robotic Limbs](/industrial-lifter-arm-right).

occurrences.label: Hackers are a relatively uncommon weapon type and rarely show up in shops (with the exception of Long Cleavers, which are commonly sold by Sheks). Low quality Flesh Cleavers can be found on [Cannibals](/cannibals) and [Shrieking Bandits](/shrieking-bandits). [Paladin's Cross](/paladins-cross) is wielded by [Paladins](/paladin), who tend to travel in large groups and have decent stats, making this an unlikely place to get hackers from. [Band of Bones](/band-of-bones) frequently wield Rusted Blade quality Combat Cleavers, making them a good source of hackers in the early game. Various medium-high quality hackers spawn via the [Artifacts](/artifacts) system.

occurrences.label: Heavy Weapons are common among Sheks and Skeletons, but rare everywhere else. You can buy Planks and Fragment Axes in [Shek Kingdom](/shek-kingdom) weapons shops. Low quality ones can be found in ruins in [Border Zone](/border-zone) and [Shek Kingdom](/shek-kingdom), as well as animal nests. Shek bandit factions [Berserkers](/berserkers) and [Kral's Chosen](/krals-chosen) often wield ancient quality Heavy Weapons, making them a good source of heavy weapons in the early game.

occurrences.label: **Meitou** (**名刀**, "Famous/Excellent Sword" in Japanese) is the highest weapon grade in the game. Only the legendary smith [Cross](/cross) has been able to craft weapons of this quality. Their weapons are spread around the land of Kenshi, often owned by important dignitaries, rich nobles, or powerful warriors.

Their weapons are spread around the land of Kenshi, often owned by important dignitaries, rich nobles, or powerful warriors.

occurrences.label: Staffs are popular among farmers and nomads, but all other polearms are quite rare. Low quality [Polearms](/polearm) are wielded by [Hive](/hive), but [their shops](/hive-trader) don't sell them (they sometimes do sell Polearm blueprints though). Most Polearm class weapons can be found in animal nests as junk loot, although they tend to spawn primarily [heavy weapons](/heavy-weapons) and [sabres](/sabres).
occurrences.literal: Staffs are popular among farmers and nomads, but all other polearms are quite rare. Low quality [Polearms](/polearm) are wielded by [Hive](/hive), but [their shops](/hive-trader) don't sell them (they sometimes do sell Polearm blueprints though). Most Polearm class weapons can be found in animal nests as junk loot, although they tend to spawn primarily [heavy weapons](/heavy-weapons) and [sabres](/sabres).

occurrences.label: All polearms spawn in the [Scraphouse](/scraphouse), which has qualities from Catun (uncommon, but they do have a chance to be Catun quality) up to Edgewalker. Staff/Naginata/Naginata Katana are also sold in the [Catun Scrapmaster](/catun-scrapmasters) shop. Other than that, they are exceedingly rare in weapon shops and very few of them spawn as [Artifacts](/artifacts) outside of late game locations.

occurrences.label: The Eagle's Cross does more damage per shot, making it a superior choice against armoured opponents, as it will overcome the target's harpoon resistance, leading to greater damage. Furthermore, a masterwork-quality bow is capable of one-shotting many enemies, including human enemies up to a moderate degrees of toughness, with light armour. If including height advantage, the Eagle's Cross is capable of doing over 200 damage to low-toughness enemies, one-shotting some [robots](/robots) when shooting from a high cliff, for example. In contrast, the Oldworld Bow MkII is generally limited to one-shotting only weak enemies with no armour.
occurrences.literal: The Eagle's Cross does more damage per shot, making it a superior choice against armoured opponents, as it will overcome the target's harpoon resistance, leading to greater damage. If including height advantage, the Eagle's Cross is capable of doing over 200 damage to low-toughness enemies, one-shotting some [robots](/robots) when shooting from a high cliff, for example. In contrast, the Oldworld Bow MkII is generally limited to one-shotting only weak enemies with no armour.

occurrences.label: Per point of damage, assuming the Eagle's Cross does 50% more damage per bolt, which is roughly accurate (it depends on the quality level).
occurrences.literal: Per point of damage, assuming the Eagle's Cross does 50% more damage per bolt, which is roughly accurate (it depends on the quality level).

occurrences.label: While the Eagle's Cross's higher damage is generally an advantage, it is a detriment in friendly-fire situations. While fighters in heavy armour can generally shrug off many accidental hits from the Oldworld Bow MkII, friendly fire from the Eagle's Cross can sometimes prove catastrophic — knocking out, maiming or even outright killing allies in a single shot. If one wants to provide supporting fire to melee fighters, with the Eagle's Cross, it is recommended to only use high-toughness melee fighters with good quality — and in particular, high coverage — armours, such as [Crab Armour](/crab-armour) with underlying [Chainmail](/chainmail) armour. Players should also consider the effect that height advantage may have on any friendly-fire damage.

occurrences.label: The Eagle's Cross does more damage per shot, making it a superior choice against armoured opponents, as it will overcome the target's harpoon resistance, leading to greater damage. Furthermore, a masterwork-quality bow is capable of one-shotting many enemies, including human enemies up to a moderate degrees of toughness, with light armour. If including height advantage, the Eagle's Cross is capable of doing over 200 damage to low-toughness enemies, one-shotting some [robots](/robots) when shooting from a high cliff, for example. In contrast, the Oldworld Bow MkII is generally limited to one-shotting only weak enemies with no armour.
occurrences.literal: The Eagle's Cross does more damage per shot, making it a superior choice against armoured opponents, as it will overcome the target's harpoon resistance, leading to greater damage. Furthermore, a masterwork-quality bow is capable of one-shotting many enemies, including human enemies up to a moderate degrees of toughness, with light armour. If including height advantage, the Eagle's Cross is capable of doing over 200 damage to low-toughness enemies, one-shotting some [robots](/robots) when shooting from a high cliff, for example. In contrast, the Oldworld Bow MkII is generally limited to one-shotting only weak enemies with no armour.

occurrences.label: Per point of damage, assuming the Eagle's Cross does 50% more damage per bolt, which is roughly accurate (it depends on the quality level).
occurrences.literal: Per point of damage, assuming the Eagle's Cross does 50% more damage per bolt, which is roughly accurate (it depends on the quality level).

occurrences.label: While the Eagle's Cross's higher damage is generally an advantage, it is a detriment in friendly-fire situations. While fighters in heavy armour can generally shrug off many accidental hits from the Oldworld Bow MkII, friendly fire from the Eagle's Cross can sometimes prove catastrophic — knocking out, maiming or even outright killing allies in a single shot. If one wants to provide supporting fire to melee fighters, with the Eagle's Cross, it is recommended to only use high-toughness melee fighters with good quality — and in particular, high coverage — armours, such as [Crab Armour](/crab-armour) with underlying [Chainmail](/chainmail) armour. Players should also consider the effect that height advantage may have on any friendly-fire damage.

occurrences.label: Stolen armour can be [dyed](/colour-scheme) resulting in a different colour scheme than the original. In order to do so a stolen or looted Empire Samurai Armour has to be sold to a vendor to clear it's colour scheme. After which the blank armour can be bought/stolen back and coloured in the usual way. Another way to clear the stolen tag is to place the armour into an [Item Furnace](/item-furnace) or a Crossbow Locker. [Samurai Gate Sergeants](/samurai-gate-sergeant) are a good "source" of specialist (10% chance of MW) quality armour. For guaranteed Masterwork quality Empire Samurai Armour, you can loot _[empire noble guard---](/sandas-noble-guard) found in Bark._

occurrences.label: Compared with [Conscript Leather Armour](/conscript-leather-armour), which on appearance should be a white version of **Mercenary Leather Armour,** they do offer different protection against blunt and cut resistance with the amount of difference being variable, depending on the grade. Harpoon resistance is the same or just one point in favour of the Mercenary version. The coverage and the skill penalties are always the same. The value of Mercenary armour is always higher than Conscript.
occurrences.literal: Compared with [Conscript Leather Armour](/conscript-leather-armour), which on appearance should be a white version of **Mercenary Leather Armour,** they do offer different protection against blunt and cut resistance with the amount of difference being variable, depending on the grade. Harpoon resistance is the same or just one point in favour of the Mercenary version. The coverage and the skill penalties are always the same. The value of Mercenary armour is always higher than Conscript.

occurrences.label: Starting the comparison at **prototype** grade, Conscript does not provide any protection all, thus is Mercenary the better choice. When quality is improved to **shoddy** grade, the Mercenary armour outclasses the counterpart with 2%, 4% more blunt and cut resistance and 1 point in harpoon resistance. At **Standard** grade, the Conscript version offers 2% more blunt resistance, at the expense of 1 point harpoon resistance, making the armour slightly better than the Mercenary version.
occurrences.literal: Starting the comparison at **prototype** grade, Conscript does not provide any protection all, thus is Mercenary the better choice. When quality is improved to **shoddy** grade, the Mercenary armour outclasses the counterpart with 2%, 4% more blunt and cut resistance and 1 point in harpoon resistance. At **Standard** grade, the Conscript version offers 2% more blunt resistance, at the expense of 1 point harpoon resistance, making the armour slightly better than the Mercenary version.

occurrences.label: Compared to **high** quality, they offer the same protection, expect harpoon resistance. From **Specialist** quality onwards, Conscript offers more blunt resistance, while Mercenary armour offers more cut resistance. The difference in protection are 2% for blunt and 4% cutting. At **Masterwork**, these differences are 4% and 5% respectively.
occurrences.literal: Compared to **high** quality, they offer the same protection, expect harpoon resistance. From **Specialist** quality onwards, Conscript offers more blunt resistance, while Mercenary armour offers more cut resistance. The difference in protection are 2% for blunt and 4% cutting. At **Masterwork**, these differences are 4% and 5% respectively.

occurrences.label: As conclusion, Mercenary is better at low qualities, near equal at standard and high quality and offers more cutting resistance at specialist and masterwork, but at these grades, offers less blunt protection compared to Conscript.
occurrences.literal: As conclusion, Mercenary is better at low qualities, near equal at standard and high quality and offers more cutting resistance at specialist and masterwork, but at these grades, offers less blunt protection compared to Conscript.

occurrences.label: The **Plate Jacket** is a Medium Armour that is equipped in the Body Armour slot. It can be normally found sold in [Mongrel](/mongrel), [United Cities](/united-cities), [Shek](/shek-kingdom), and [Tech Hunter](/tech-hunters) armour shops. It is one of the only body armours that covers 100% of the entire upper body. It is the worst of the three plate jackets, suffering from the Stealth and Assassination penalties that the black variant is free of, while also sharing the same inferior Dexterity penalty compared to the white variant. It also suffers from a 1% worse Cut Resistance across its Specialist and Masterwork grades.

occurrences.label: [Armour](/armour) is clothing which provides armour protection in battle. Heavier armour provides more protection, however it also detracts from other [Statistics](/statistics), such as run speed and stealth. Armour can be purchased from stores, stolen, or found in ancient locations such as [Lost Armouries](/lost-armoury) and [Ancient Labs](/ancient-labs). After some researching, armour can be created at a [Leather Armour Crafting Bench](/leather-armour-crafting-bench), [Chain Armour Crafting Bench](/chain-armour-crafting-bench), or [Heavy Armour Smithy](/heavy-armour-smithy). The quality of [Homemade](/homemade) armour is exclusively dependent on the character's [Armour Smith](/armour-smith) level.

occurrences.label: Splint Kits are used to temporarily give HP to significantly damaged organic limbs. If a limb falls below 50 health, a Splint Kit can be used to fix it. Splinting can only be used if the unit has bandaged health on them. (Having 0 health due to 100 stun damage will not allow you to splint) The splint kit currently comes in two different sizes. You can splint up to your field medic skill, with a cap of the quality + 1. (Advanced capping at 51 rigged health, normal kit 26)

occurrences.label: First Aid, Splint and Skeleton Repair Kits possess a quality modifier, which must be met by your [Field Medic](/field-medic) or [Robotics](/robotics) skills to be effectively used. Having a higher skill also reduces the speed in which the Kit will be used up. Lack of lighting will only reduce the robotics skill, but injuries reduce both field medic and robotics. The reduction is -0.45% skill for every 1% max hp in damage received on a character's head. To give an example, a Greenlander with 80 damage done to their head will have -36% Field Medic/Robotics (0.45x80).

The reduction is -0.45% skill for every 1% max hp in damage received on a character's head. To give an example, a Greenlander with 80 damage done to their head will have -36% Field Medic/Robotics (0.45x80).

caption: "A splint kit can be used to rig up wounded bodyparts so that they can be used again.  Useful if you have a leg injury and don't want to limp all the way back to town, you can splint up your leg and regain a little functionality.

They also have the bonus that any splinted damage counts against limb amputation in combat.

The amount of hitpoints you can splint is limited by your medic skill and the quality of the kit."

occurrences.label: **Trade Goods** are items generally meant for trading, crafting or other uses depending on the item. They buy and sell for their full value unlike most other items, which tend to sell for a much lower value, and are often either ingredients or craftable themselves. [Stolen](/thievery) trade goods, however, will sell for half the price, like most other items. The value at any given town is randomized from town to town to allow for players to make profit via trading between them, though the value is still restricted to +/- 30% from the base value. Some towns also have an additional modifier to specific goods to make them worth more or less there.

occurrences.label: Characters can get in trouble in [The Holy Nation](/the-holy-nation) when having Robot Limbs. They will be seen as Skeletons and attacked unless the Holy Nation [faction reputation](/guide-to-faction-relations) is 50 or higher. Even if the reputation is 50 or higher, a character wearing robotic limbs will be unable to interact with [Holy Lord Phoenix](/holy-lord-phoenix) and any other member of the Holy Nation including [Paladins](/paladin), [Holy Priests](/holy-priest) and Shopkeepers (taking off robotic limbs would nonetheless still allow). The Holy Nation trade caravans who patrol around can still be traded with even without allying with their faction.

occurrences.label: **Clothing** is any [equipment](/equipment) which can be equipped in an armour slot but gives no defensive bonus and does not fall into the [Light](/light-armour), [Medium](/medium-armour), or [Heavy](/heavy-armour) armour class. Many serve no purpose beyond decreasing your "looks like a slave" rating when escaping [Slavery](/slavery). Clothing tends to be found as starting gear on new recruits. Some clothing may provide bonuses to [Athletics](/athletics), [Combat Speed](/combat-speed), [Stealth](/stealth), or [Martial Arts](/martial-arts).

occurrences.label: **Light Armour** are items which can be equipped on a character which offer armour protection without adding too much weight to the wearer. This armour tends to provide buffs to stats to compensate for the lack of protection as compared to medium and heavy armour.
occurrences.literal: **Light Armour** are items which can be equipped on a character which offer armour protection without adding too much weight to the wearer. This armour tends to provide buffs to stats to compensate for the lack of protection as compared to medium and heavy armour.

occurrences.label: A large portion of light armour consists of items made out of [Leather](/leather). Unlike [Clothing](/clothing), most light armour must be learned through a [Blueprint](/blueprints). Light armour can be made with a [Clothing Bench](/clothing-bench), [Leather Armour Crafting Bench](/leather-armour-crafting-bench), or a [Heavy Armour Smithy](/heavy-armour-smithy).
occurrences.literal: A large portion of light armour consists of items made out of [Leather](/leather). Unlike [Clothing](/clothing), most light armour must be learned through a [Blueprint](/blueprints). Light armour can be made with a [Clothing Bench](/clothing-bench), [Leather Armour Crafting Bench](/leather-armour-crafting-bench), or a [Heavy Armour Smithy](/heavy-armour-smithy).

occurrences.label: **Trade Goods** are items generally meant for trading, crafting or other uses depending on the item. They buy and sell for their full value unlike most other items, which tend to sell for a much lower value, and are often either ingredients or craftable themselves. [Stolen](/thievery) trade goods, however, will sell for half the price, like most other items. The value at any given town is randomized from town to town to allow for players to make profit via trading between them, though the value is still restricted to +/- 30% from the base value. Some towns also have an additional modifier to specific goods to make them worth more or less there.

occurrences.label: Like all weapons, attack speed, with heavy weapons is determined by a combination of having enough [Strength](/strength) to use it effectively, [Dexterity](/dexterity), as well as [Melee Attack](/melee-attack). Block speed is determined by a combination of having enough Strength to use it effectively, Dexterity, as well as [Melee Defense](/melee-defense). The base attack speed is 0.765, every level in Dexterity will increase this by 0.00228, and 0.00152 for attack. Strength comes into play in the required strength level of the weapon, if below its required level your combat speed will be penalized (up to -47.5% at 20 levels or more below). Strength above the required level does not affect speed at all, beyond acting as a buffer for injuries penalizing your strength. The strength requirement to use a weapon is the blunt damage multiplied by 40[1].

There are some minor exceptions to this rule, like when the result is lower than the default weight of the weapon. A weapon's weight\_mult and weight\_kg can be observed in FCS.

occurrences.label: They feature a two-hit combo attack (called Downward Combo) that makes them particularly useful when fighting animals or singular weak opponents but leaves their wielder vulnerable to getting hit in battles with multiple foes. The combo attack is the only weapon animation[1] which has less than 100 power (100% of the weapon's damage). It makes up for this by attacking twice: the power of the first strike is 80 and the second one is 60. Unfortunately, though, Downward Combo is usually too slow_\[clarify\]_ to land the second hit on an opponent if they were staggered by another attack. This leads to overall less damage over time when compared to weapon types like [Sabres](/sabres) or [Polearms](/polearms)[2].
